actors.name: Emeric

entries.look: A half-elf in road-stained leather with a lute on a frayed strap, mid-gesture, about to say something.
entries.bio: He was not born to the troupe, he was left with it. Half-elf children turn up in towns neither parent stayed long in, and a travelling company that needed a boy to hold horses did not ask questions. He learned lute, dice, three accents, and how to read a room before he learned to read.
entries.ties: The company broke apart when he was in his twenties — over money, or over a woman, depending on which version he is telling. He has worked alone since, which suits him considerably less than he lets on. He tells people he prefers the freedom. He is looking for them, and has never said so out loud.
entries.goal: To be the reason a room changes its mind. What he is actually good at is noticing; he will tell you it is the music, but the music is only the reason to be in the room.
entries.hooks: He remembers what people want and is usually glad to help them get it, which is generous and occasionally a problem — Halia will find that out before he does. Give him rooms rather than fights. Agatha at Conyberry is his scene: a performance for her earns a second answer outright. If the troupe ever turns up, do not announce it.

actors.note: Your own character. Point him at other people's moments, not his own.

actors.name: Amryn Velaris

entries.look: A high elf who stands where the light is worst, and looks like she is about to try something.
entries.bio: High elf wizard, chaotic neutral, one hundred and fifteen years old and barely an adult by elven reckoning. Old bloodline, one of the mountain strongholds, and every expectation that she would fall in line with the lawful orders. She wanted the primal stuff instead — fire and ice pulled straight from the source, no safety net.
entries.ties: She tried it. It levelled her family's laboratory and killed several conclave elders. Her standing was stripped, her family disowned her, and she was run out. She lives in the shadow of a mountain city that does not ask questions, and finds chaos suits her better than their rules ever did.
entries.goal: To reach the raw thing she was reaching for the first time, and survive it. And to find out who wrote the older hand — in the water-damaged spellbook, and on Don-Jon's map, in the same script.
entries.hooks: Fragile: threaten her with position, not damage. She is reckless and knows it, so give her chances to be reckless where the cost is visible in advance. The unrecognised handwriting is her thread — do not resolve it this campaign. Somebody from the conclave is still looking for her.

actors.note: 14 hp. Anything that threatens the paladin removes her in one turn. Ranged problems and cover, never a melee rush.

actors.name: Levi White

entries.look: A high elf in gold, and audible from a long way off. The greatsword is lit from inside.
entries.bio: High elf paladin, lawful good, and the fourteenth child of the royal house of Aurelion — a family in which only one heir is meant to survive to inherit. He was raised to fight his siblings and trained his whole life for the day he would have to kill them.
entries.ties: Outsiders invaded Aurelion and killed his father. Standing over the king's last breath beside his brother Callum, a beam of holy light came through the ceiling, took hold of Levi, and set him down in a country he had never seen.
entries.goal: To find out why the light chose him rather than any of the others, get home, and take back the throne. He has not decided what he owes his surviving siblings, and the question follows him.
entries.hooks: Level six against level twos. Never scale monsters up for him, that kills the rest — split objectives instead and give him the thing only he can hold. His whole life was a fight he was told he had to win alone; give him a choice where winning alone is the wrong answer. Do not hand him Icehewer.

actors.note: Level 6 against level 2s. Never scale monsters up to challenge him, that kills the others. Split objectives instead.

entries.look: A wood elf in furs with a two-headed axe across her back, checking the exits before the chairs.
entries.bio: Wood elf, soldier, chaotic good. Raised in a forest village where music and stories filled the trees, she followed her parents onto the road as a travelling entertainer, village to village, song to song.
entries.ties: War found the village. It was destroyed and her family vanished with it. She joined the army out of grief and anger, learned the axe she named Thornsong, and refused every order that would have harmed the innocent — which made her reckless in the reports and beloved in the ranks. She left when the war ended.
entries.goal: To make sure nobody else loses what she lost, and to keep hold of the entertainer she was before the war took a run at her.
entries.hooks: Give her the tracking, the weather and the terrain reads — she should be the one who notices the migration first and gets to be right about it. She was a performer before a soldier: put her in a room with Emeric and let them work it together. An order that would cost innocent people is the fastest way to find out who she is.

entries.truth: A coward who knows it. He would rather send strangers to die than admit the town has no plan.
entries.leverage: Challenge him in front of another townsperson and he folds completely.

entries.truth: Gustaf Stellern. He built the lodge with his own hands after a life he does not describe, and the name Falcon came with him from it. He has seen a dragon before. He is the only person in this valley who is not surprised.

'Gustaf,' he says, to nobody. 'Nobody's called me that in eleven years.'

actors.name: Cryovain

entries.look: White. Larger than the barn it is standing on. Unhurried.
entries.lore: Arcana DC 12: a young white dragon. Simple, territorial, vain. Hunts by cold and patience, not cunning.

narration: It does not roar. It exhales, and the sound is a door opening in a cold house.
The snow ahead of it stops falling. It is freezing in the air.
It banks once overhead, close enough that you feel the pressure change, and does not attack. It is counting you.
Frost spreads where it lands, and keeps spreading after it has stopped moving.
It takes the roof off without appearing to try.
actors.note: This is the whole campaign. Every appearance before the last should end with it leaving of its own accord. KILLED, THEY GET: the hoard in the hollow at the top of the Hold, already placed on that map — 220 gp, plate, buckles and a hunting horn — plus a frost-blue scale cut from the body (GIVE item.scale). The scale is what Harbin pays the full commission against, so raise it before they walk away from the body. DRIVEN OFF INSTEAD: the hoard is still there and still theirs and Phandalin still pays in full, but the dragon is alive somewhere north. That is the ending this adventure is built for and it is worth the same coin.

He says a word in Orc, and every one of them stops at once.
