Melee, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing.
Melee, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing.
Ranged, +5 to hit, range 100/200. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Already dead at Umbrage Hill. Kept here because they will want to examine the body, and because you may want a second one later.

actors.note: ALREADY DEAD at Umbrage Hill. THEY GET: a frost-blue scale out of the wound (GIVE item.scale), which is not the manticore's and is the first hard proof in the campaign. Nothing else. Do not point at it; let them search the body.

actors.name: Wolf pack

entries.look: Thin. Too thin for this time of year.
entries.tracks: Survival DC 10: they have been ranging much further south than they should be.

narration: They are not growling. That is the part that should worry you.

stats.summary: Medium beast, unaligned — wolf (run 3–5 of them)

sections.label: Traits
rows: Advantage on Perception checks relying on hearing or smell.
Advantage on an attack if an ally is within 5 ft. of the target and not incapacitated.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing. DC 11 Strength save or knocked prone.

sections.label: Running it
rows: They are starving, not hunting. Food, or an Animal Handling check, ends this without a round of combat.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: pelts worth 2 gp each and nothing else. FED INSTEAD: they scatter and the party learn from Falcon that eleven farms have gone quiet, which is the actual prize. Animal Handling DC 12 sees they are starving rather than hunting.

actors.name: Giant boar

entries.look: Something between a pig and a landslide.

sections.label: Traits
rows: If it moves 20+ ft. straight at a target and hits with a tusk attack, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) slashing and must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or be knocked prone.
Relentless (recharges after a short or long rest)
Damage that would reduce it to 0 hp leaves it at 1 hp instead if the damage was 10 or less.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Give it a straight run. Charge is the whole creature.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: 60 lb of meat, worth 15 gp in Phandalin or a great deal of goodwill given out free.

actors.name: Ankheg

entries.look: The ground opens and something segmented comes out of it.
entries.lore: Nature DC 12: it hunts by vibration. Standing still works. Running does not.

narration: The ground goes soft under someone, and then it is not ground.

meta: darkvision 60 ft., tremorsense 60 ft., passive Perception 11

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing plus 3 (1d6) acid. A Large or smaller target is grappled (escape DC 13) and restrained; the ankheg can then only bite that target, with advantage.
30 ft. by 5 ft. line. DC 13 Dexterity save, 10 (3d6) acid, half on a success. If it is grappling a creature it cannot use this.

sections.label: Running it
rows: It hunts by vibration. Standing still works, running does not, and that is worth telling them on a Nature check.
Never appear where they are looking. Come up under whoever moved last round.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: nothing on it. Dig out the burrow beneath the stacks and there is everything it has dragged down over a season: 55 gp, a logger's tally stick (GIVE item.tallystick), and three bodies the camp will want back.

actors.name: Merrow

entries.look: It came out of the surf and it should not be able to stand up like that.
entries.lore: Nature DC 12: sea ogres. They do not come this far north unless something moved them.

narration: The harpoon line goes taut and somebody's feet leave the stone.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing.
Melee, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) slashing.
Melee or ranged, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing. A Huge or smaller target must succeed on a DC 16 Strength contest or be pulled up to 20 ft. toward the merrow.

sections.label: Running it
rows: The harpoon drags people off the rocks. The fight is the drop, not the damage. Cold water this far north is a countdown, not a swim check.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: 20 gp of drowned coin in a net bag, and harpoons worth 5 gp each. In the shallows where they were holding station: the keeper's lantern, thrown from the tower (GIVE item.lantern).

entries.look: Something behind the wall has been running for years.
entries.detail: A water wheel driving nothing at all. The output shaft has been cut through, cleanly, recently.
entries.truth: Gnerkli cut it. The noise was covering sounds from below and he needed to hear them.

entries.look: A standing stone, split top to bottom, ice in the crack.
entries.detail: Elvish, older than the road. It marks a boundary with nothing on the other side of it any more.
entries.truth: Free reward for an all-elf party. Any of them reads it without a check: 'past here, we did not go.'

entries.look: A farm cart, tipped, half-buried.
entries.detail: The traces are cut, not broken. Somebody unhitched the horse and ran.
entries.truth: Nessa's cart. Put it where they will find it before they meet her.

entries.look: Iron bands, a good lock, and no dust on the lid.
entries.detail: The lock has been picked already, badly, and re-closed.
entries.truth: Whoever opened it first took one thing and left everything else, which is the interesting part.

entries.look: A basin of water that has not frozen, in a building with no roof.
entries.detail: The water shows the room you are standing in, one heartbeat late.
entries.truth: Savras. It answers one true question per party and the answer is never the useful one.

actors.name: Goblin

entries.look: Small, fast, and already moving to somewhere you are not looking.
entries.lore: Nature DC 10: they will not hold a line. They will leave and come back with friends.

narration: It shoots, then disappears behind the rock it was already standing near.

sections.label: Traits
rows: Takes the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing.
Ranged, +4 to hit, range 80/320. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Shoot, hide, repeat. Never let one stand still and trade hits — that is the whole creature.
Six weak goblins in cover beat two strong ones in the open. Use cover, not hit points.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: 1d10 sp each and a crude weapon. TAKEN ALIVE: it gives up everything immediately, means it, and will lead them to the strongbox. One live goblin is worth more than six dead ones.

actors.name: Bugbear

entries.look: It was in the room before you were and you did not see it.
entries.lore: History DC 11: goblins obey them out of straightforward fear.

narration: The first you know of it is the reach.

sections.label: Traits
rows: A melee weapon deals one extra die of damage (included below).
If it surprises a creature and hits on the first turn, the attack deals an extra 7 (2d6).

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) piercing.
Melee or ranged, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Worth 2d6 exactly once. Spend it on the opening round or not at all.
Stealth +6 on something with a morningstar. Open at reach, from cover, on whoever is furthest back.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: 35 gp, a morningstar worth 10 gp, and the key to Grol's war chest on a thong round its neck.

actors.name: Twig blight

entries.look: A bundle of dead sticks, and then it is not.
entries.lore: Nature DC 12: they grow where something has poisoned the ground. Fire ends them fast.

narration: The undergrowth stands up.

meta: understands Common but does not speak

sections.label: Traits
rows: While motionless, indistinguishable from a dead shrub.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Run eight. They are a terrain problem, not a threat.
Vulnerable to it. Give the wizard the round she has been waiting for.

actors.note: DESTROYED, THEY GET: nothing. They burn well and the fire tells Venomfang exactly where the party are, which is the cost. Say the smoke goes straight up.

actors.name: Agatha

entries.look: An elf, or the shape of one, hanging a few inches above the leaf litter.
entries.rumour: They say there is a banshee in the wood east of Conyberry who answers one question.
entries.voice: Perfectly courteous, and about two centuries out of date.
entries.truth: She answers one question truthfully if offered a gift she considers beautiful. She has been dead long enough to be bored, not cruel.
entries.leverage: A comb, a mirror, a song. Emeric performing for her is worth more than treasure.

narration: She asks, politely, whether you have brought her anything.

meta: acid, fire, lightning, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks
cold, necrotic, poison; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralysed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained

sections.label: Traits
rows: Senses living creatures within 5 miles and knows their kind.
Moves through creatures and objects as difficult terrain; 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (3d6 + 2) necrotic.
Each non-undead within 60 ft. that can see her: DC 13 Wisdom save or frightened for 1 minute.
Every creature within 30 ft. that can hear her and is not undead: DC 13 Constitution save or drop to 0 hit points.

sections.label: Running it
rows: This is a negotiation with a stat block attached. The Wail is there so the table understands the stakes of getting it wrong.
A gift she finds beautiful buys one true answer. Let Emeric try a song and reward it outright.

actors.name: Venomfang

entries.look: Green, coiled in a tower that used to have a roof, entirely unbothered by you.
entries.lore: Arcana DC 13: a young green dragon. Green ones talk. That is what makes them dangerous.

narration: It does not attack. It asks you a question, and waits, and appears genuinely interested in the answer.
It offers you a deal, and the deal is good, and that is the problem.
actors.note: Far above them. Venomfang is a conversation, not an encounter. If they fight, it kills someone and leaves. KILLED, THEY GET: this should not happen at these levels. If it somehow does — 300 gp of scattered hoard in the tower and a water-damaged spellbook (GIVE item.spellbook). TALKED PAST INSTEAD: it lets them take the spellbook and walk out if they tell it one true thing about Cryovain it did not already know. Same item, nobody dies, and it costs them nothing but information.

stats.summary: Large dragon (chromatic), lawful evil — young green dragon
meta: blindsight 30 ft., darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 17

sections.label: Actions
rows: One Bite and two Claw attacks.
Melee, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing plus 7 (2d6) poison.
Melee, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing.
30-foot cone. DC 14 Constitution save, 42 (12d6) poison, half on a success.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Always. It wants information and it wants to be flattered, in that order.
It is CR 8 against level 2s. Kill one character, then leave. Do not soften it, and do not let it become a grind.
It will trade safe passage for something it wants. Let that be a real option they can take.

actors.name: Elmar Barthen

entries.look: Lean, greying, wearing an apron over good clothes. Writes while he talks to you.
entries.rumour: Barthen's will front you supplies on a promise. Nobody knows how he stays solvent.
entries.voice: Kind and unhurried, and he finishes his sentence before he looks up.
entries.truth: He fronts supplies because he remembers arriving here with nothing. He is quietly the reason four families have not left.
entries.leverage: He is the only person in town who calls Falcon by his birth name. Ask him about Gustaf Stellern and he will tell you more than Falcon ever would.

narration: He writes the whole order down before he tells you he cannot fill half of it.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +2 to hit. Hit: 2 (1d4). He is not a combatant.

sections.label: Running him
rows: Credit, a cart, an ox, and directions. The practical spine of every expedition.
He knew Gustaf before the lodge. He will not gossip, but he will confirm.

actors.name: Sister Garaele

entries.look: A young elf keeping a shrine to Tymora that is cleaner than anything else in Phandalin.
entries.rumour: She goes away for days at a time and comes back with mud on boots that should not have mud on them.
entries.voice: Warm and precise. Asks you a question back, every time, and means it.
entries.truth: Harper. She is gathering what is happening in this valley and sending it east, and she is doing it alone.
entries.leverage: She will trade information for information, straight across, and she will keep her half of it.

narration: She looks at the party for a beat too long, the way somebody does when they are memorising you.

sections.label: Traits
rows: 1st-level cleric. DC 12, +4 to hit. Cantrips: light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy. 1st (3 slots): bless, cure wounds, sanctuary.

sections.label: Running her
rows: Your party is four elves in a human town. She is the one person who does not find that remarkable, and that will land.
Do not confirm it this campaign. Let her be helpful and slightly too well informed.

actors.name: Dazlyn Grayshard

entries.look: A shield dwarf in a dig trench, filthy to the elbow, entirely happy.
entries.rumour: She has been digging at that hillside for two seasons and has not sold a single thing out of it.
entries.voice: Fast, delighted, and technical. Assumes you find this as interesting as she does.
entries.truth: She is not looking for ore. She is looking for the layer underneath the dwarven work, and she has found it.
entries.leverage: Show any real interest in the older stonework and she will tell you everything, at length, immediately.

narration: She keeps talking while she climbs out of the trench, and does not repeat the part you missed.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +2 to hit. Hit: 3 (1d6) piercing. It is a tool, not a weapon.

sections.label: Running her
rows: The elvish layer beneath the dwarven layer. Your all-elf party will read it before she can.
Do not let it happen offscreen. She should be alive when they arrive and it should be their choice.

actors.name: Miraal

entries.look: A woman in a roofless shrine, standing in water that has not frozen, answering a question you have not asked.
entries.rumour: There is a shrine north of the road and something in it still speaks.
entries.voice: Answers the question you are about to ask. Do this exactly twice, then stop doing it.
entries.truth: Genuinely prophetic and genuinely unwell. Savras gives her true things in the wrong order, and she has stopped being able to tell which order she is living in.
entries.leverage: None. She wants to be useful and cannot control when she is.

narration: She answers before you finish asking.
'That one,' she says, pointing at whichever player has said the least. 'It matters that you were here.'
actors.note: The orcs took the shrine from her. If the party clears it she stays, and becomes the one person who can tell them where the dragon is without them having to look.

stats.summary: Medium humanoid (human), neutral — acolyte of Savras

sections.label: Traits
rows: 1st-level cleric. DC 13, +5 to hit. Cantrips: guidance, sacred flame. 1st (3 slots): bless, cure wounds, detect evil and good.
Once per day she can answer one question truthfully. She cannot choose which day.

sections.label: Running her
rows: One true question per party, and the answer is never the useful one. Write it down before they interpret it.
Do not play her as mad
She is correct. That is what makes it uncomfortable.

actors.name: Moesko

entries.look: An orc in soaked robes on a headland, with the storm arranging itself around him.
entries.rumour: Something on the coast has been calling things up out of the water for a month.
entries.voice: Calm, courteous and completely certain. He will explain what he is doing if asked.
entries.truth: Anchorite of Talos. He is not raiding — he is keeping a promise. Talos took his people's mountain and gave them the storm instead.
entries.leverage: He cannot be bargained with, but he can be understood, and understanding him is what makes the orcs at the ranch and the shrine make sense.

narration: He does not stop the ritual to talk to you. He talks to you while continuing it.
actors.note: The theological spine of the whole adventure: the dragon took Icespire Hold, the orcs lost their home, and the ones who did not scatter turned to the god of destruction.

stats.summary: Medium humanoid (orc), chaotic evil — anchorite of Talos

sections.label: Traits
rows: As a bonus action, moves up to its speed toward a hostile creature it can see.
4th-level cleric. DC 13, +5 to hit. Cantrips: resistance, shocking grasp, thaumaturgy. 1st (4 slots): fog cloud, thunderwave. 2nd (3 slots): gust of wind, warding bond.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning.

sections.label: Running him
rows: He will answer honestly. The party learns why there are orcs everywhere, from the orcs.
On a ledge above cold water, thunderwave is not damage. It is a fall.

actors.name: Talon Thornwild

entries.look: A woman at the treeline who has been watching the stone circle for two days and has not slept.
entries.rumour: A druid has been asking in Phandalin whether anyone has heard thunder without weather.
entries.voice: Clipped. Gives you the situation and not the pleasantries.
entries.truth: She has tracked the anchorites here and cannot stop the ritual alone. Asking for help costs her something.
entries.leverage: Be useful once and she is an ally for the rest of the campaign.

narration: 'You hear that?' she says. There is no thunder. Then there is.

sections.label: Traits
rows: 4th-level druid. DC 13, +5 to hit. Cantrips: druidcraft, produce flame, shillelagh. 1st (4 slots): entangle, longstrider, speak with animals, thunderwave. 2nd (3 slots): animal messenger, barkskin.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +2 to hit (+5 with shillelagh), reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d6) or 6 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning.

sections.label: Running her
rows: She fights beside them and lets them decide. Never let her win the scene.
If the circle holds, she owes them, and she is the one who can find things in the Neverwinter Wood.

actors.name: Anchorite of Talos

entries.look: An orc in soaked robes, unarmoured, and entirely unbothered by the weather.
entries.lore: Religion DC 12: priests of the storm god. They do not raid for food. They raid because destruction is the prayer.

narration: The thunder arrives a beat before the gesture that caused it, which is the wrong way round.

sections.label: Traits
rows: As a bonus action, moves up to its speed toward a hostile creature it can see.
4th-level cleric. DC 13, +5 to hit. Cantrips: resistance, shocking grasp, thaumaturgy. 1st (4 slots): fog cloud, thunderwave. 2nd (3 slots): gust of wind, warding bond.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Cast on another orc before the fight. Half the damage goes to the anchorite — tell the table when they notice, not before.
Every anchorite in this campaign lost the same mountain. Play them as bereaved, not evil.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: 25 gp, a storm-marked talisman worth 30 gp to the right buyer, and a written list of the valley's shrines with three crossed off.

actors.name: Wererat

entries.look: A miner, until the shape of the face stops being a face.
entries.lore: Nature DC 12: lycanthropes. Ordinary weapons slide off them. Silver does not.

narration: It speaks while it changes, and finishes the sentence afterwards in a different voice.

meta: bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered

sections.label: Traits
rows: Can turn into a rat-humanoid hybrid or a giant rat, or back.
Advantage on Perception checks relying on smell.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Two attacks, only one of which may be a bite.
Melee, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing. A humanoid must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution save or contract wererat lycanthropy.
Ranged, +4 to hit, range 30/120. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing.

sections.label: Running it
rows: A party with no silvered or magical weapon cannot hurt them. Establish that in round one and let the fight become a negotiation.
They were driven out of the Shrine of Savras by orcs. They want their home back and will trade the mine for it.
Do not infect a PC casually. If you do, mean it and play it out.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: 40 gp each in the lower gallery and the mine's paychest key. Silver or nothing — anyone who bought a silvered dagger in Phandalin gets to feel clever (item.silverdagger). NEGOTIATED WITH INSTEAD: they hand over the mine and 90 gp to be left alone, and they keep their word.

actors.name: Gorthok the Thunder Boar

entries.look: A boar the size of a cart, wreathed in lightning that is not touching it.
entries.lore: Religion DC 14: an avatar of Talos. Not summoned so much as invited, and it stays as long as it is interested.

narration: It does not charge. It walks, and the ground reports it.
Lightning leaves it rather than striking it.
actors.note: Far above them. Gorthok is a disaster to be interrupted, not a boss to be fought. Break the ritual and it goes. BROKEN OFF, THEY GET: nothing on the boar — it comes apart into weather. On the ritual ground where it stood: 50 gp of offerings the anchorites piled there, and a tusk the length of a forearm, still warm, worth 25 gp to anyone in Phandalin who wants proof of what was up here. KILLED OUTRIGHT INSTEAD: exactly the same, and Talos notices. Say the thunder follows them a full day south.

sections.label: Traits
rows: If it moves 20+ ft. straight at a target and hits with a tusk attack, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) and must make a DC 16 Strength save or be knocked prone.
Relentless (recharges after a short or long rest)
Damage that would reduce it to 0 leaves it at 1 hp instead, if the damage was 25 or less.

sections.label: Actions
rows: One tusk and one lightning strike.
Melee, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) slashing.
One creature within 60 ft. DC 15 Dexterity save, 22 (4d10) lightning, half on a success.

sections.label: Running it
rows: CR 7 against your table is a wipe. The scene is the ritual, and the ritual can be broken.
Down the anchorites, or break the pillars, and Gorthok loses interest and leaves. Say so in the fiction early.

actors.name: The shade in the barrow

entries.look: Cold in the shape of a man, standing over a sword he will not pick up.
entries.lore: History DC 13: Tanamere Alagondar, a prince of old Neverwinter, buried with the blade he killed a dragon with.

narration: It does not attack. It looks at whoever is holding a weapon, and waits.
'It is not a gift,' it says. 'It is a duty. Do you understand the difference.'
actors.note: Play it as a test, not a fight. If the party states plainly that they mean to kill the dragon, it stands aside. STOOD ASIDE, THEY GET: Icehewer, handed over rather than taken (GIVE item.icehewer), and he tells them plainly where the dragon lies up. FOUGHT AND PUT DOWN INSTEAD: the same blade off the bier and 30 gp of grave goods, but nothing said and nothing learned. The blade is theirs either way; what fighting costs them is the directions.

stats.summary: Medium undead, lawful neutral — the barrow's keeper
meta: acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder; nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing
necrotic, poison; charmed, exhaustion, grappled, paralysed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 18 (4d8) necrotic, and DC 13 Constitution save or hit point maximum is reduced by the damage until a long rest.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Always. A party that answers honestly never rolls initiative here.
Dragon Slayer. It is the whole point of the barrow, and it should cost a promise rather than a fight.

entries.look: A campaign chest, iron-bound, and the lock is better than the chest.
entries.detail: Sturdy, scratched at the hasp where somebody has opened it often in a hurry. DC 15 Thieves' Tools, or he opens it if asked outright and trusted.
entries.truth: Inside: the knotted cord, a bundle of letters he never sent, and a second bow wrapped in oilcloth that belonged to somebody else.

entries.look: A clothes chest at the foot of a bed, lid down, not locked.
entries.detail: Folded clothes, all sizes, and a child's slate with three letters practised on it.
entries.truth: The slate is the hook. A child got out of this ranch and nobody in Phandalin has reported one missing.

entries.look: Stores on racks with dates chalked on the rails.
entries.detail: Salt pork, roots, apples in sand. The dates run to yesterday.
entries.truth: Somebody worked down here right up until it happened, which puts the attack inside a day.

actors.name: The door in the back wall

entries.look: A plank door in the back wall of the cellar, barred on this side.
entries.detail: There is no matching door on the outside of the house. Whatever it opens onto is under the hill.
entries.truth: This is the manor tunnel network reaching further than anyone thinks. Do not open it this session.

entries.look: A writing desk half out of the ruined door, drawer shut.
entries.detail: Dry inside, which it should not be. A candle stub, paper, and a small iron key.
entries.truth: The key fits the door beneath the cellars. Whatever barred that door barred it from the far side.

entries.look: Crates and barrels stacked six high along the east shelf.
entries.detail: Six months of food for a warren that no longer needs six months of anything.
entries.truth: They keep stocking for thirty. Nobody has adjusted the order.

entries.look: A stone plinth on a red rug, four braziers burning around it, and a red crystal on top.
entries.detail: The crystal is the only red thing in Gnomengarde and it was carried in from outside.
entries.truth: Nobody will say who tends the braziers. The answer is Gnerkli, every night, and he will not say why either.

entries.look: Sorted rubble, stacked by hand, graded by size.
entries.detail: Somebody sorts this by eye as it comes out. In the deepest heap there is worked stone that is not dwarven.
entries.truth: Elvish, and finer than the dwarven work above it. This is the second spine of the campaign.

entries.look: Suits of plate along both walls of the hall, upright after a century.
entries.detail: Bound, not undead. They are watching a line scored across the floor rather than the room.
entries.truth: Cross the line and they move. Walk round it and they do not. The solution is visible on the floor.

entries.look: A dry stone bowl worn into shape by hands rather than water.
entries.detail: One question, one true answer, and no promise the answer helps.
entries.truth: Answer honestly at the table even when it wrecks your plan. Fudge it once and the shrine is worthless forever.

entries.look: A brass sea-lamp, full of oil, wick cut short.
entries.detail: Whole, fuelled, and deliberately put out.
entries.truth: The keeper cut his own wick and walked down off the rock. He was not taken.

entries.look: Two hundred bunks, every one stripped to the boards.
entries.detail: No bedding, no kit, no bodies. Under one bunk, a bracer left behind in the hurry.
entries.truth: They packed and went out another way. Nobody died in this room.

entries.look: A working shelf of remedies, labelled in a small careful hand.
entries.detail: Tonics, salves, and a second set of instruments sized for a child's hands, never used.
entries.truth: Her mother taught her on those. Her mother is under the floor. Do not volunteer this.

entries.look: Nine notices, four of them the same job in different hands.
entries.detail: Harbin writes them out himself. The repeated one has no date on it any more.
entries.truth: He stopped dating it because the date was starting to look like an accusation.

entries.look: Elvish tombs, lids carved with a hand older than the fortress above.
entries.detail: The dwarven fortress was built straight over these without moving one of them.
entries.truth: Whoever built above knew what was below and chose to leave it. Same mason's mark as the excavation.

entries.look: Loose turf at the foot of the northern stone, recently lifted.
entries.detail: A oilcloth roll: tindertwigs, a flask, and a coin nobody uses any more.
entries.truth: Somebody has been sheltering in the ring and leaving supplies. They are still alive.

actors.name: Starving wolf

entries.look: Ribs showing, and it is watching the party rather than circling them.
entries.lore: Animal Handling DC 12: starving, not hunting. Food ends this without a fight.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: a pelt worth 2 gp. FED INSTEAD: nothing material, and Falcon notices, and Falcon is worth having.

actors.name: Stirge

entries.look: A thing like a mosquito the size of a cat, hanging from the ceiling.
entries.lore: Nature DC 10: they drink and drop off. Killing them mid-drink hurts the host.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: nothing at all. They drink and drop off; killing one mid-drink hurts whoever it is on. This is an attrition encounter, not a treasure one, and the party should feel that.

actors.name: Orc scout

entries.look: Posted badly, facing north, and not watching the road at all.
entries.lore: Insight DC 11: it is not looking for the party. It is watching the sky.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: 2d6 gp, a bow worth 10 gp, and it was watching the sky rather than the road. Insight DC 11 gets that for free before anyone rolls initiative.

actors.name: Goblin lookout

entries.look: On the plank bridge, bored, and it has not seen you.
entries.lore: It will bolt and raise the alarm rather than fight. Catching it is the encounter.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: 1d10 sp. CAUGHT INSTEAD: it names the dammed stream above the cave, which floods the lower passages in seconds and is worth more than the whole hideout's coin.

actors.name: Carrion ravens

entries.look: A dozen of them, in the trees, and none of them are coming down to the body.
entries.tracks: Survival DC 10: they will not land on it. Whatever killed it is close enough that they will not risk it.

actors.note: KILLED, THEY GET: nothing, and they should feel slightly bad. The point of the ravens is that they will not land on the manticore. Survival DC 10 gets that.

entries.look: A shipping crate, lid nailed rather than hinged.
entries.detail: Prying it costs a crowbar or a Strength check. The nails are new and the wood is not.
entries.truth: Inside: tindertwigs, a coil of rope, and a sealed tin of lamp oil — the last one for a hundred miles.

entries.look: A barrel with the head pushed in.
entries.detail: Salt pork under a crust of frost, still good, and something wrapped in oilcloth at the bottom.
entries.truth: Give them four days of rations and, one time in three, a silver coin nobody uses any more.

entries.look: An iron-strapped box the size of a breadbin, locked.
entries.detail: DC 15 Thieves' Tools, DC 17 to force, or the key is somewhere in this building.
entries.truth: Coin, a deed to an empty house in Phandalin, and a letter that names somebody the party have already met.

entries.look: Somebody died here and nobody came back for them.
entries.detail: Weeks old, in the cold. Still holding what they were holding.
entries.truth: Whatever they carried is intact. Use it to hand over one thing the party actually need, and let the corpse be the reason it is free.

entries.look: A traveller's pack, straps cut rather than unbuckled.
entries.detail: Somebody got out of it fast and did not come back. Contents untouched.
entries.truth: Rations, a waterskin, a bone whistle, and a hand-drawn chart with farms crossed off it.

entries.look: Shelving, part-stripped, and what is left is arranged to look like more.
entries.detail: Whoever keeps this took what they could carry and squared off the rest.
entries.truth: One useful consumable. Do not itemise the whole shelf; give them the one thing and move on.

entries.look: A niche cut into the stone at shoulder height.
entries.detail: Dry, swept, and out of the line of sight from the door.
entries.truth: Somebody cached something here on purpose: a flask, a stub of candle, and a key that opens a door elsewhere on this map.

entries.look: Stones stacked deliberately, not fallen.
entries.detail: Recent. Somebody built this in the last month and did not have long.
entries.truth: Under it: a wrapped bundle. Whoever built it meant to come back, and did not.

entries.look: Rubble where a wall came down, and the fall looks wrong.
entries.detail: It fell inward. Moving it takes two people and ten minutes.
entries.truth: Under the stone, unless that placement says otherwise: 2d6 gp of household coin and whatever the room lost when the roof came down. It is rubble, not a puzzle — the specific placement carries anything that matters.

entries.look: A bench with the work still on it, mid-job.
entries.detail: Tools laid out in order. The job is half finished and the chair is pushed back.
entries.truth: Tinker's tools, usable, and whatever the job was is the clue: read it and hand it over.

actors.name: The Black Knight

entries.look: Black plate, matte and unreflective, with a long sword point-down in front of him and both gauntlets resting on the pommel. He is a head and a half taller than any of you. There is no surcoat, no device, no mark of a house. Where the visor is open there is nothing behind it, and the nothing is not dark: it is simply absent, the way a doorway with no room behind it is absent.
entries.lore: The last warden of the Long Span, set to hold the toll-gate by people who then cut the bridge out from under him and left. Three hundred years of holding a gate on a road to nowhere. He is not evil, he is not cursed in the usual sense, and he has no idea that the war he is still fighting ended before Phandalin had a name.

narration: "The toll." The voice comes from inside the armour and arrives a half-beat late, as though it had to travel. "The toll, and you may cross."
He does not raise the sword. He lifts it, which is a different motion, and it is the motion of a man who has done it ten thousand times and never once enjoyed it.
"There is no crossing." A pause. "I am aware. The toll, and you may cross."
He steps over the fallen one without looking down, and moves to the next of you, and the sword comes up again at exactly the same angle.
When the blow lands he says, quietly, as though to somebody else entirely: "It is a good road. It goes all the way to the sea."
actors.note: He does not kill. Mechanically: when a character drops to 0 he immediately disengages from them and moves to another target, he never attacks an unconscious creature, and he never pursues below the top tier. Say this with his behaviour and never announce it. He has one real weakness and it is not martial: any sincere offering, any object handed over as a toll, costs him his next action while he tries to remember what to do with it. A party who work that out can win this without a single death on either side, and that is the best ending available. BEATEN, THEY GET: the warden’s reliquary on the top tier behind him, already placed on that map — 240 gp, a silvered dagger and a hunting horn. TOLLED INSTEAD: the copper token in the last occupied parapet niche on the first tier is the thing he has been waiting three hundred years to be handed, and he will not ask for it by name. Given it, he stands down, gives up the reliquary himself, and walks off the bridge going south. Same loot, no initiative rolled, and it is the better ending.

meta: Elvish, Common; he answers in whichever he was last addressed in
The top tier of the Long Span

sections.label: Traits
rows: He cannot move below the top tier under any circumstance, and he cannot be moved there. Anyone who climbs back down has left the fight.
He never attacks an unconscious creature, and on reducing a creature to 0 hit points he must move to a different target on his next turn.
If a creature offers him an object as a toll, using its action to do so sincerely, he loses his next action. This works once per creature and there is no saving throw.

sections.label: Actions
rows: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., 1d10 + 4 slashing. He fights at reach because he is enormous, not because the blade is.
He grounds the sword. Each creature within 15 feet makes a DC 13 Strength save or is knocked prone and has its speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. No damage.

entries.look: A row of shallow stone niches along the inside of the first-tier parapet, most of them empty.
entries.detail: The stone inside them is less weathered than the stone around. Three have fresh scratches. One still has something in it.
entries.truth: They were toll niches. Travellers left something and crossed. The one still occupied holds a copper token with a road stamped on it, which is the thing the knight is waiting for and will not ask for by name.

entries.look: Stencilled crate, lid prised and re-nailed.
entries.detail: Salt, lamp oil, hard bread. The re-nailing is fresh.
entries.truth: Somebody has been living out of these and putting them back so it does not show.

entries.look: A grain sack, tied at the neck, heavier than grain.
entries.detail: Cut it and something that is not grain comes out first.
entries.truth: Whoever packed this was leaving and changed their mind about what mattered.

entries.look: Under a bunk, dragged out and shoved back.
entries.detail: Kit, a spare shirt, and a letter nobody sent.
entries.truth: The letter names somebody in Phandalin. Use it when you need a personal reason.

entries.look: A slotted box by a shrine, unlocked, and nobody has emptied it.
entries.detail: Coppers, a silver, and one thing that is not money.
entries.truth: Nobody has taken from this. That is the story of the place in one object.

entries.look: One board sits proud of the others by a hair.
entries.detail: A gap under it, dry, with something in it.
entries.truth: Where people put the thing they would not want found by whoever came through the door.

entries.look: Damp-swollen books, most of them ruined.
entries.detail: Three are readable. One is not a book.
entries.truth: Three readable volumes, worth 10 gp to a collector in Neverwinter and nothing here. The fourth is a hollowed binding holding a house deed (GIVE item.deed) unless that placement names something else.

entries.look: A workman's chest, lid open, tools in their slots.
entries.detail: Everything is in its place except one empty slot.
entries.truth: Whatever came out of that slot was taken in a hurry and is somewhere else on this map.

entries.look: Somebody did not get out, and their pack is still on.
entries.detail: Rations gone off, a bedroll, and something they were carrying home.
entries.truth: Unless that placement names them, this is Emmet Kirk, a Phandalin carter who took the north road in the first week and did not come back. Barthen carried him on credit and will want to know. On him: 2d6 gp and his half of a delivery tally.

entries.look: Ash, banked and gone out days ago.
entries.detail: Something in the ash that did not burn.
entries.truth: Paper does not fully burn. Neither does bone.

entries.look: Stone rim, rope down, bucket at the bottom.
entries.detail: The rope is newer than the well and the bucket is not the original.
entries.truth: Things get dropped in wells to be rid of them. Reward anyone who hauls it up.

entries.look: Stone, worn, and not dedicated to anything anyone here worships.
entries.detail: Offerings on it that have not rotted, which at this age they should have.
entries.truth: The elvish layer again. Same hand as the excavation and the undercroft.

entries.look: A ledge nobody looks at, at head height, inside the door.
entries.detail: Dust everywhere except one clean patch.
entries.truth: Where you put a key you want findable by somebody who knows, and invisible to somebody who does not.

items.name: Icehewer
items.text: A dwarven battleaxe with frost worked into the blade, and a haft wrapped in something that is not leather.
items.detail: The runes down both bits are Dwarvish and they are not decoration — they are a sentence, and it is a boast. The wrapping on the grip is white dragon hide, scaled and iridescent, and it is always slightly cold to hold.
items.secret: From the Dragon Barrow. Do not hand it to Levi. Make the party decide who needs it, out loud. The cold bonus is a trap: Its extra damage does nothing to the dragon it was forged for. Let a player discover that mid-fight rather than telling them. Who holds it: Do not hand it to Levi. Make the party decide out loud who needs it, and let that conversation be the reward.

meta: The burial chamber under the Dragon Barrow

sections.label: Properties
rows: You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon.
On a hit, the target takes an extra 1d6 cold damage. Creatures immune to cold take none, and Cryovain is immune to cold.
While held, you are unharmed by temperatures as low as −20 degrees Fahrenheit. It does not warm you — it simply stops the cold mattering.

sections.label: What it says
rows: 'I was made for the thing that made this cold.' Any dwarf reads it without a check. Anyone else needs Dwarvish.

items.name: A water-damaged spellbook
items.text: A water-damaged spellbook, swollen at the spine. Three pages are still legible.
items.detail: Mage armour and feather fall, written in a careful trained hand. Then a third page, loose, in a different hand entirely — older, faster, and Elvish. Whoever wrote the book was copying from something they did not fully understand.
items.secret: The unrecognised hand is Elvish and older than the book. It matches the second drawing on Don-Jon's map. Amryn's thread: She is the one who should notice the hands do not match. Give her the check, or give it to her free.

meta: Water-damaged; the rest of the book is a solid block
The flooded lower room of the Woodland Manse

sections.label: Contents
rows: 1st level. Copyable into a wizard's own book at the usual cost and time.
Not a spell. A diagram, in Elvish, in a hand older than the book.

sections.label: The third page
rows: The same hand as the second drawing on Don-Jon's survey map. The party has now seen it twice.
A cross-section of something beneath a valley, drawn by somebody who had been down there.
Not this campaign. Two sightings and no answer is the correct amount.

items.name: Gauntlets of ogre power
items.text: Leather and iron, much heavier than they look.
items.detail: Strength becomes 19 while worn. Attunement.
items.secret: Give these to Amryn's player rather than the obvious owner and watch what the table does with it. Give them wrong: Hand these to Amryn's player rather than the obvious owner and watch what the table does with it.

meta: Icespire Hold, or wherever you choose to place it

sections.label: Properties
rows: Your Strength score is 19 while you wear these. They have no effect if your Strength is already 19 or higher.

items.name: Cloak of the winter hare
items.text: White fur, and it never seems to be wet.
items.detail: Advantage on Stealth in snow. Once per dawn, take the Dash action as a bonus action.
items.secret: Falcon made it and will not say from what. If asked directly he changes the subject exactly once. Where it came from: Falcon made it and will not say from what. If asked directly he changes the subject exactly once.

meta: Falcon gives it, or it is taken from his loft

sections.label: Properties
rows: Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made in snow.
Once per dawn, take the Dash action as a bonus action.

items.name: Gnomish far-lens
items.text: Brass, articulated, and it clicks when you fold it.
items.detail: Doubles the range at which you can make a Perception check by sight. It also whistles, faintly, and cannot be stopped.
items.secret: Gnomengarde reward. The whistle matters if they try to hide from something with good hearing.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Advantage on Perception checks that rely on sight at long range.
Dropped on stone, it breaks. The gnomes will make another, once.

items.name: A coil of gnomish rope
items.text: Fifty feet, and it coils itself when dropped.
items.detail: It knots on command and unknots on a different command that nobody wrote down.
items.secret: The second command word is in Gnerkli's handwriting on a scrap in the store room. Let them find it later.

sections.label: Properties
rows: On command, it knots or unknots itself at one end.
It obeys twice a day and then sulks, which is the gnomes' word, not yours.

items.name: A plain silver ring
items.text: Sized for someone with narrow hands.
items.detail: Warm to the touch when worn. Advantage on saves against being frightened.
items.secret: From the Manse. It is elven and it was left behind on purpose, which is the interesting part.

sections.label: Properties
rows: You are unharmed by temperatures as low as −20 degrees.
Whoever wears it sleeps badly and does not know why.

items.name: A single white scale
items.text: The size of a dinner plate, cold to hold, and staying cold.
items.detail: It does not warm up. Left in a bowl of water overnight, the water freezes solid around it.
items.secret: Physical proof, so the argument in Phandalin stops being about whether and starts being about what to do.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Hard evidence of a white dragon, and the first anyone in Phandalin has seen.

items.name: An unsent letter
items.text: Found in the ranch house. Two lines in, the handwriting changes speed.
items.detail: Addressed to Neverwinter. 'Take them and go. I will follow when the cattle are down.'
items.secret: Big Al Nabber wrote it to his sister in Neverwinter the morning the orcs came over the ridge, and never sent it. His wife Nessa and their daughter got out through the cellar door; he stayed for the cattle. Show it to him and he will not take it back, and he will ask whether anyone has seen a girl of nine. That girl is the one who practised three letters on the slate and sat in the dark by the salt.

sections.label: Properties
rows: The handwriting changes speed two lines in.

items.name: Halia's ledger page
items.text: A single torn page of accounts.
items.detail: Three Phandalin names, three sums, and beside each a date that has not happened yet.
items.secret: Give this to one player and nobody else. The Zhentarim thread works best as one person's problem.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Four, with running totals, and one of them is not a debtor.

items.name: Nessa's charm
items.text: A bent nail on a bootlace. She gave it to you.
items.detail: She says her mother said it keeps the cold off. It does not.
items.secret: Worth nothing. Worth everything at tick eight. If a PC is wearing it when the dragon comes, say so.

sections.label: Properties
rows: A child, badly, and kept anyway.

items.name: Four sets of gnomish tools
items.text: Recovered, and none of them belong to anyone still alive.
items.detail: Each has a name scratched into the handle. Bexley. Torren. Wibbet. Anneth.
items.secret: Four sets, belonging to Fimble, Dabble, Nim and Corsin Waggletop, the four gnomes the mimic took. Say the four names aloud, one at a time, when the party hand them back. The warren sets four more places at the table that night and nobody explains it.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Proficiency with tinker's tools applies. Four sets means four owners, and there are four empty places at the table.

items.name: A tally stick
items.text: Notched wood from the loggers' camp.
items.detail: Nineteen notches, then a gap, then four more in a different hand.
items.secret: Tibor Wester kept notching it for eleven days after the crew walked south, so the count would look right when his cousin the townmaster asked. The crew's half went south with them. Put the two halves together and the eleven days of lies are visible without a word being said.

sections.label: Properties
rows: One half of a split stick. The other went south.

items.name: A shed antler, cracked through
items.text: Found on the road north.
items.detail: It did not break on a tree. It broke from the inside, from freezing.
items.secret: Nature DC 13. A quiet way to make the cold feel like an agent rather than weather.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Not shed cleanly. Something took it off.

items.name: An orcish effigy
items.text: Bound sticks and hide, made in a hurry.
items.detail: It has wings, and someone has driven a nail through them.
items.secret: Yargath's people made it in the first week at the ranch. It is a ward against the cold, not against people — they were as frightened of what came down the mountain as the ranchers were. Showing it to Yargath before drawing a weapon is worth a free round of honest conversation.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Made in a hurry, and it is a ward against cold rather than against people.

items.name: Axeholm's keyring
items.text: Four iron keys on a ring, all of them cold.
items.detail: Three fit doors you have seen. The fourth does not fit anything above ground.
items.secret: Nine keys. Eight open the gates, halls and armoury of Axeholm. The fourth from the ring's clasp opens the cistern, which is where the cold shade is. Do not point at it; let them try keys until one turns.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Most of Axeholm. Not the cistern.

items.name: A surveyor's map
items.text: Don-Jon's, covered in his handwriting.
items.detail: The excavation is drawn twice: once as dug, and once as it apparently should have been.
items.secret: The second drawing is older than the mine and not in his hand. It matches the Manse spellbook page.

sections.label: Properties
rows: The dig, drawn accurately, and one line drawn beneath it in a different hand.

items.name: Harbin's writ of commission
items.text: Official, stamped, and worth exactly as much as Phandalin's authority.
items.detail: It entitles the bearer to requisition from the town stores. Once.
items.secret: Cash this in during the evacuation. It is the only concrete thing Harbin ever gives them.

sections.label: Properties
rows: It is worth exactly as much as the person reading it thinks Phandalin is worth.

items.name: A deed to an empty house
items.text: Phandalin, one storey, needs a roof.
items.detail: Harbin hands it over instead of coin when the coin runs out.
items.secret: A stone house on the north side of Phandalin's square, standing, empty, and in the name of a family that left two winters ago. Harbin will sign it over for 50 gp or for one more job. It is a base, a reason to care whether the town survives, and somewhere to put the people from the farms when the clock runs on.

sections.label: Properties
rows: It is standing, it is empty, and the deed is in somebody else's name.

items.name: What the font said
items.text: Written down, because nobody trusted themselves to remember it.
items.detail: 'It will not be the cold that takes the town.'
items.secret: Whatever the party asked, the font answered truthfully and unhelpfully. The words it gave them become correct at tick seven of Cryovain's clock, and not before. Write down what you said and read it back to them word for word when the seventh tick lands.

sections.label: Properties
rows: True, unhelpful so far, and it will be helpful later.

items.name: Two potions of healing
items.text: Adabra's. She will not take payment.
items.detail: 2d4+2 each. She has more, and she will keep giving them away.
items.secret: Restock these whenever the party visits her. It makes the windmill worth defending.

items.name: A skin of Phandalin firewine
items.text: Toblen's, and stronger than it has any right to be.
items.detail: Advantage on the next save against cold within the hour. Also, disadvantage on everything else, briefly.
items.secret: Play the downside honestly and they will use it exactly once, at the right moment.

sections.label: Properties
rows: A draught wards off cold for an hour. Two and you are no use to anyone.

items.name: Three jars of gnomish pitch
items.text: Sealed, heavy, and warm through the glass.
items.detail: Thrown: 2d6 fire in a 5 ft square, and it keeps burning for a minute.
items.secret: The only ranged answer the party has to something that will not land. Make sure Gnomengarde offers it. Why it matters: The only ranged answer this party has to something that will not land. Make sure Gnomengarde offers it.

meta: Gnomengarde, as payment or as a gift

sections.label: Using it
rows: Ranged attack against AC 12. On a hit, 2d6 fire in a 5-foot square, and it burns for 1 minute.
Anything entering the square or ending its turn there takes 1d6 fire.

items.name: Cold-weather rations
items.text: Linene's, at a markup she will not apologise for.
items.detail: A week each. Without them, travel north of the lodge costs exhaustion.
items.secret: Four days for four people. This is the only resource worth tracking in this campaign — track it out of Phandalin and nothing else, and stop tracking it once they have a base.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Keeps in frost. Tastes of it too.

items.name: A whistle that makes no sound
items.text: Bone, worn smooth, found in the barrow.
items.detail: Blowing it does nothing you can hear. Every dog and wolf within a mile turns to look at you.
items.secret: It works on the wolves at the lodge, and on nothing else. Let them discover the limit themselves. The limit: It works on the wolves at Falcon's lodge and on nothing else in this campaign. Let them find the edge themselves.

meta: The antechamber of the Dragon Barrow

sections.label: Properties
rows: Blowing it produces no sound audible to humanoids. Every dog and wolf within a mile turns toward it.

items.name: A cup from the Manse table
items.text: Still where somebody set it down.
items.detail: Elven, unremarkable, and the water in it has not evaporated in three hundred years.
items.secret: If a PC drinks it, nothing happens, and they dream of the house as it was. Give that to one player privately.

sections.label: Properties
rows: It was on the table when they left, and it has been there since.

items.name: A tarnished brooch
items.text: A hawk in flight, badly repaired at some point.
items.detail: Company of the Yellow Banner. Falcon's, or it was.
items.secret: He left it in the lodge deliberately. Returning it is worth more to him than gold.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Under it, elvish work, and older than the town.

items.name: A child's slate
items.text: From one of the northern farms.
items.detail: Somebody was practising letters. The last word is unfinished.
items.secret: It is Nessa Nabber's daughter's, age nine, practising the first three letters of her own name. She hid in the ranch cellar by the salt and walked out on her own. She is alive, on the Neverwinter road, and will turn up in Phandalin two sessions from now. Do not say any of that at the table — let Big Al recognise the slate.

sections.label: Properties
rows: The start of a name that is not on any body here.

items.name: The butter ledger
items.text: A slate in the cellar with dates chalked on it in rows.
items.detail: The rows run to yesterday. Somebody was working down here the morning it happened.
items.secret: Big Al kept working while his family hid under his feet. He will not say that, and the dates say it for him.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Yesterday, which puts the attack inside a day.

items.name: A bundle of spare shafts
items.text: From Falcon's loft. Straight, matched, and far more than one man needs.
items.detail: Twenty arrows' worth, fletched and ready. He will give them away without being asked twice.
items.secret: He has been provisioning for a siege for months. Let the party notice the quantity, not the quality.

sections.label: Properties
rows: A bow nobody at this table owns.

items.name: A mason's mark, cut out of the lintel
items.text: A hand-sized piece of dressed stone, prised out of a doorway in the undercroft.
items.detail: A single mark in a fast Elvish hand. The same hand as the loose page in the water-damaged spellbook, and the second drawing on Don-Jon's survey map. Three times now, on three things that should have nothing to do with each other.
items.secret: Do not answer this. Three sightings and no resolution is exactly right for one campaign — it is the thread you pull in the next one. If Amryn's player asks directly, tell them the hand is older than everything it has been found on, and leave it there.

stats.summary: Wondrous item, no magical properties whatsoever
meta: The lintel over the undercroft stair, Icespire Hold

sections.label: What it is
rows: The signature a builder cuts into their own work.
On a loose page in the Woodland Manse spellbook, and on Don-Jon Raskin's survey map.
The same person marked an elven crypt beneath Icespire Peak, a page older than the book it was in, and a dig at the other end of the valley.

items.name: Adabra's tonic
items.text: A stoppered clay bottle, warm to hold, smelling of rosemary and something sharper underneath.
items.detail: Two doses. A dose restores 2d4+2 hit points and tastes appalling. Adabra makes them four at a time and will not sell them to anyone going north; she gives those away.
items.secret: Adabra makes four at a time and gives them away to anyone going north. If the party pay for these she is insulted, quietly, and they will not notice. Hand one over the first time somebody is hurt in front of her.

items.name: Frost salve
items.text: Grey paste in a tin, and it goes on cold before it goes on warm.
items.detail: Ends one level of exhaustion from cold, or gives advantage on the next save against cold for an hour. One use. Adabra has three left and cannot make more until the road opens.
items.secret: She has three and cannot make more until the road opens, and she will still give all three away. That is the character in one object. Do not have her explain it.

sections.label: Effect
rows: Ends one level of exhaustion caused by cold, or grants advantage on the next saving throw against cold damage within the hour.

items.name: Bundle of tindertwigs
items.text: Twenty slivers of resinous pine in an oilcloth roll.
items.detail: Lights a fire in one round in any weather. Barthen throws these in with a sale and does not charge for them.
items.secret: Barthen puts these in the sack without charging. If a player notices and tries to pay, he waves it off and changes the subject to the weather.

sections.label: Properties
rows: A fire in one round in any weather.

items.name: Barthen's road rations
items.text: Hard bread, smoked fish, dried apple, packed tight in waxed cloth.
items.detail: Four days for four people. Barthen packs them himself and puts more in than he charges for.
items.secret: He packs more than he charges for, every time, for everyone. It is why his ledger looks the way it does.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Elmar, who puts in more than he charges for.

items.name: Last of the lamp oil
items.text: A sealed tin, heavier than it looks.
items.detail: Six hours of lantern light, or a flask thrown for 1d6 fire and a burning square. There is no more of this in Phandalin and Barthen will not say so.
items.secret: This is the last tin in Phandalin and Barthen will say it is 'on order'. It is not on order. The road it comes down is closed.

items.name: Garaele's flask
items.text: A flat silver flask with Tymora's coin stamped on the face.
items.detail: Holy water, properly made. She gives it to people going somewhere she cannot follow, and she keeps a list of who has one.
items.secret: She keeps a list of who has one of these and where they went. If the party ask why, she tells them the truth: so that somebody knows.

items.name: Bone comb
items.text: An elvish comb in white bone, three teeth missing, worn smooth at the spine.
items.detail: From the manse. Older than the house. Somebody carried this a long way and then set it down and left it.
items.secret: Older than the manse by centuries. Whoever carried it set it down on a north-facing sill and walked away, which is what everybody in that house seems to have done.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Older than the house, and the house is old.

items.name: A candle stub and a blanket
items.text: A wool blanket folded small, and a candle burnt to the last half inch.
items.detail: From the ranch cellar. Somebody sat in the dark here for hours, out of the line of the stair, and then walked out. The blanket is child-sized.
items.secret: Child-sized blanket, hours of wax, and crumbs. Somebody small hid here through the whole thing and then walked out on their own. Do not answer where they went. Not this session.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Somebody small sat here in the dark for hours and walked out on their own.

items.name: A coin nobody uses
items.text: A silver coin, thin, worn nearly smooth, with a tower on one face.
items.detail: Neverwintan, minted before the eruption. Barthen has seen four of these this month and all of them came down from the north.
items.secret: Barthen has taken four of these this month and all four came from people arriving from the north with nothing else to pay with.

items.name: Frost-blue scale
items.text: A single scale the size of a dinner plate, edged like a blade and cold to the touch.
items.detail: Off the manticore at Umbrage Hill, embedded in the wound. It is not the manticore's. Whatever this came off is very large and very cold, and any dragon-lore at all names the colour.
items.secret: Not the manticore's. White dragon, and a big one. This is the first hard proof in the campaign and it is sitting in a wound at the very first job. Let them find it. Do not point at it.

sections.label: Properties
rows: It does not warm up in a closed hand.
White dragon, and a large one. The first hard evidence in the campaign.

items.name: A notice off the board
items.text: A job notice in the townmaster's hand, written out and posted four separate times.
items.detail: Same job, four weeks running, nobody took it. Harbin has stopped writing a date on it.
items.secret: Four weeks, four postings, nobody took it. Harbin stopped dating it because the date was starting to look like an accusation.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Same job, four weeks, no date on the last one.

items.name: Knotted cord
items.text: A leather cord with eleven knots in it, found on the lodge table.
items.detail: Falcon counts something with this. Eleven so far. He will not say eleven of what until somebody asks him twice.
items.secret: Eleven knots. Eleven farms. He has been counting them since the first one went quiet and he has told nobody, because telling somebody would make it a thing he has to act on.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Eleven farms gone quiet, and he has told nobody.

items.name: The desk key
items.text: A small iron key from the drawer of a desk standing in a ruined doorway.
items.detail: It fits nothing in the manor above ground. It fits a door under the cellars, and the door is on the wrong side of its own bar.
items.secret: It fits a door beneath the manor cellars that is barred from the wrong side. The key is for getting in. Whatever barred it wanted out.

meta: Tresendar Manor, the desk in the doorway

sections.label: Properties
rows: A door beneath the cellars, barred from the far side.

items.name: Tally stick
items.text: A split hazel stick, notched, one half only.
items.detail: The logging camp's count. The notches stop eleven days ago and the matching half went south with the crew.
items.secret: The matching half went south with the crew. If the party ever find it, the two halves together are the only proof that Tibor knew before he said he knew.

items.name: A hand-drawn chart
items.text: Oilcloth, drawn in three different inks by three different hands over a long time.
items.detail: The roads north, with farms marked. Somebody has been crossing farms off. The crossings-off are recent and they run south towards Phandalin in order.
items.secret: The crossings-off run south in order and the order is a timetable. Laid next to the clock, it tells you roughly how long Phandalin has.

sections.label: Properties
rows: They run south, in order, and the order is a timetable.

items.name: Circle stone
items.text: A pebble from inside the standing stones, warm in a closed hand.
items.detail: While carried, you always know which way is north, and you sleep undisturbed by weather. It is not magic anyone can identify, and it stops working if taken out of the valley.
items.secret: It stops working outside the valley and nobody can identify it, including a wizard. That is deliberate. Do not explain the stones this campaign.

sections.label: Effect
rows: While carried, you always know which way is north.
You are not woken by weather.
It does nothing outside the valley.

items.name: Dwarf-cut bracers
items.text: Plain steel bracers from Axeholm, unmarked, and lighter than they should be.
items.detail: AC 12 + Dex if unarmoured. Made for somebody with shorter arms; whoever wears them has to have them refitted, and the only smith within a week is in Phandalin.
items.secret: Made for a dwarf. Fitting them costs a day in Phandalin and the only smith is behind on work, which is a way to put the party in town when something happens there.

sections.label: Fitting
rows: Cut for a dwarf. They must be refitted by a smith before they work for anyone taller, which costs a day in Phandalin.

items.name: The keeper's lantern
items.text: A brass sea-lantern with a cut wick and a full reservoir.
items.detail: Burns for eight hours on a fill and will not blow out in any wind. The keeper cut the wick himself before he left, which is the part worth thinking about.
items.secret: The keeper cut his own wick before he left. He was not taken. He put the light out on purpose and walked down off the rock, and nobody has found him.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Cannot be blown out by wind of any strength.
Eight hours on a single fill.

items.name: A cut purse
items.text: A leather purse, drawstring gone, coin still in it.
items.detail: 18 gp, 40 sp, and a token that is not currency.
items.secret: It was Emmet Kirk's, a Phandalin carter who went north in the first week of the cold and did not come back. Barthen carried his family on the ledger and will go quiet if it is brought in. Returning it to Barthen is worth more than the 18 gp: he tells them which farms have stopped sending, in order, which is the same information as the chart.

items.name: A silvered dagger
items.text: A dagger with the edge silvered, kept oiled.
items.detail: 1d4 piercing, counts as silvered.
items.secret: The mine. Anyone who thought ahead about lycanthropes gets to feel clever; anyone who did not gets a second chance here.

items.name: A climber's kit
items.text: Pitons, rope, harness, all of it used and all of it sound.
items.detail: Advantage on climbs with a surface to set a piton in.
items.secret: Falcon's spare. He hands it over without being asked if they mention the mountain.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Advantage on Athletics to climb prepared surfaces.

items.name: A smoke pot
items.text: A clay pot of damp powder with a fuse through the stopper.
items.detail: Thrown, it fills a 15-foot cube with smoke for a minute.
items.secret: Gnomish, made for a festival that did not happen. They will make two more if asked politely and four if the party bring back the four sets of tools.

sections.label: Properties
rows: Heavily obscured for 1 minute, or until strong wind.

items.name: A vial of antitoxin
items.text: A stoppered vial, bitter smelling.
items.detail: Advantage on saves against poison for an hour.
items.secret: Adabra makes these and does not sell them. She hands them to people going north.

items.name: A signet ring
items.text: A heavy ring with a worn device: a tower over water.
items.detail: Nobody in Phandalin recognises the device. Barthen goes quiet when he sees it.
items.secret: Tresendar — the family that held Phandalin before the first burning. It fits the seal on the crypt door under the manor cellars and on the correspondence in Cragmaw Castle, which is how those two threads join. Do not explain that this session; let the matching seal do it.

items.name: A hunting horn
items.text: Brass-bound, a hand span across, and it still works.
items.detail: Heard for two miles. Everything within that distance knows where you are.
items.secret: Two miles, in every direction. Falcon answers it and so does everything else on that stretch of mountain. Using it summons him in 1d4 hours and rolls one wandering encounter, and the party should be told both halves before they blow it.

items.name: A healer's kit
items.text: Bandages, splints, a suture needle, ten uses.
items.detail: Stabilise a dying creature with no check.
items.secret: The single most useful thing the party can carry at this level and nobody ever buys one.

items.name: A cask of dwarven ale
items.text: A small cask, sealed with wax and a maker's stamp.
items.detail: Worth 20 gp in Phandalin, and worth far more to the right dwarf.
items.secret: Worth 20 gp in Phandalin. Given to Don-Jon's crew at the excavation it is worth far more: they stop being contacts and become friends, which means they will dig where the party ask and send word down the valley when something moves.

items.name: An old iron key
items.text: A key too big for any door in this building.
items.detail: It fits something older and lower down.
items.secret: It opens the barred door in the back wall of the ranch cellar and the crypt door under Tresendar Manor, which are the same lock cut by the same hand. That is the first hard evidence that the tunnels under Phandalin run further than the manor. Hand it over whenever they find it; both doors stay shut without it.

scenes.name: The Sword Coast North
scenes.description: Snow to the treeline, bare rock above it. Three roads meet in the low ground and Phandalin sits where they do.

entries.label: Opening the map
entries.text: The cold has stopped behaving like weather. It does not lift at noon. It sits on the valley with weight, and the smoke from Phandalin goes straight up because there is no wind left to move it.
One hex on the map is five miles. Phandalin to Icespire Peak is most of a day.
entries.label: If anyone asks how far

entries.text: The old road north is faster, but it runs under open sky the whole way.
entries.label: If they choose a route

entries.text: Livestock have been found split open and not eaten.
entries.label: Nature DC 13

entries.text: The woods have gone quiet in a way that is wrong for the season.
entries.label: Survival DC 12
A night on the road
entries.text: You get the fire lit on the third attempt. Above the treeline the sky is the clean, hard black you only get in a hard winter, and there are more stars than any of you have seen this far south. Some time before dawn, the person on watch notices that they have stopped hearing anything at all.

entries.label: On the road, the first day
entries.text: The road climbs. Pine gives way to rock and back to pine, and the ruts under your boots are two weeks old and going the other way. Twice you stand aside for nothing, out of habit, because a road this size should have something on it.

entries.label: When Icespire first comes into view
entries.text: The cloud tears open around midday and there it is, further off than it has any right to look and still filling a third of the sky. There is new snow on it down to the treeline. It is the wrong month for that by six weeks.
Every cart on the road is going south, and every driver is loaded for a move rather than a trip.
entries.label: First hour on the road

entries.text: Nobody is cutting wood, burning charcoal, or running a trapline anywhere along the road.
entries.label: First night camping, or if they mention the quiet
A farm off the road
entries.text: A farmhouse a quarter mile off the track, door shut, stock gone, nothing broken. It has been empty about two weeks and nobody burnt it.
The road is empty in a way that is not peaceful. No carts coming south, no woodsmen, no charcoal smoke. You have been walking half a day and the only tracks in the mud are yours.
entries.label: Perception DC 10

entries.text: There is shelter if you want it, but everything that would normally use that shelter has already gone. You will sleep warm and you will sleep alone.
entries.label: Survival DC 11

entries.text: This is autumn weather in a month that should not have it yet. The cold came from the north and it came early, and the animals believed it before the people did.
entries.label: Nature DC 11

entries.text: Something passes overhead. No wingbeat: the sound is the air closing behind it.
entries.label: Perception DC 14

entries.text: This is not a season. Something is holding it here.
entries.label: Arcana DC 13

Ask whoever tracks to read the season
Follow a track rather than a road
Push on through the night, and pay for it
Ask what an elf remembers about winters here
Leave the road and find a farm
