checks.success: The road is empty in a way that is not peaceful. No carts coming south, no woodsmen, no charcoal smoke. You have been walking half a day and the only tracks in the mud are yours.
checks.failure: Cold, quiet, and a long way between anything. Nothing you can point at.

checks.when: Making camp, finding a route, or reading the country.
checks.success: There is shelter if you want it, but everything that would normally use that shelter has already gone. You will sleep warm and you will sleep alone.
checks.failure: You make camp. It is cold and it is fine.

checks.when: On the woods, the weather, or anything living.
checks.success: This is autumn weather in a month that should not have it yet. The cold came from the north and it came early, and the animals believed it before the people did.
checks.failure: Hard country. It is always hard country up here.

checks.success: Everything is moving south, and moving early. Nothing is moving north.
No predator does this. It is not feeding. It is marking.
Something passes overhead. No wingbeat: the sound is the air closing behind it.
This is not a season. Something is holding it here.

checks.when: On a frozen carcass by the road
checks.success: It froze standing up. Whatever happened, happened faster than falling over.

cues.text: Ask one player what their character does with their hands. Cold is a behaviour, not a number.
Nothing. Every time, until the once when there is something.
An elf reads it without a check. Let whoever speaks Elvish translate it aloud.

cues.when: If they push north off the road
cues.text: Let them. The country is empty, not hostile. The payoff for wandering is finding a farm already abandoned, door shut, stock gone. No fight. Just the shape of what is happening.

cues.when: If they ask how far anything is
cues.text: Everything is a day. Phandalin to Umbrage Hill is a day. Umbrage to the Excavation is a day. Never make travel the interesting part unless they make it the interesting part.
One free atmosphere beat per night and no more. Something overhead, tracks in the morning, a fire seen far off and gone by dawn. Never attack the camp in the first session.

tokens.note: A wardstone at the crossroads, elvish, older than the road. Nothing to take. Touching it in a storm is safe and the party will not know why.
A cairn beside the track with a name scratched on the top stone. Six copper left on it by somebody going south. Leave them.
A pack dropped in the ditch: bedroll, a child's boot, and a hand-drawn chart with farms crossed off in order going south. GIVE: item.chart.
A second pack, cut open by animals. Food gone, 3 gp in the lining they missed.
A carter, two weeks dead, under his own cart. Frostbitten through the coat. GIVE: item.scale if they look at the wound.
A crate fallen off a southbound wagon and never retrieved. Lamp oil, four tins, and nobody in Phandalin has any. GIVE: item.lampoil.
A rockfall across the old spur road. Under it: a milestone, elvish, pointing at nothing that exists now.

A farm cart tipped into the ditch, traces cut rather than broken — somebody unhitched the horse and ran. GIVE: nothing on it. This is Nessa’s cart: put it in front of them before they ever meet her and she is already a person when they do.

prep.threat: Exposure, and whatever is flying.
prep.wrong: The animals left weeks before the people noticed.
prep.notes: Travel is where the clock ticks. Never let a journey be free of information.

scenes.name: Phandalin
scenes.description: A mining town rebuilt on the bones of an older one. Mud, sled tracks, woodsmoke. Nobody here is older than the buildings and the buildings are not old.

entries.label: Arriving
entries.text: Conversation stops as you come up the road and starts again a beat later in a different key. Four elves is the most interesting thing to happen to Phandalin this month, and everybody has decided at once to pretend otherwise.
Townmaster Harbin Wester posts jobs on a board and does not leave the hall.
entries.label: The moment they reach the square

entries.text: Refugees have started arriving from the northern farms.
entries.label: Persuasion DC 13

entries.text: There are more empty houses here than people to fill them, and nobody mentions it.
entries.label: Investigation DC 12
Coming back, later
entries.text: There are more people in the square than there were, and fewer of them are working. Somebody has nailed boards over the north-facing windows of the Sleeping Giant, which is not a thing that helps, and everybody has looked at it and nobody has said anything.

entries.label: The square, once they stop walking
entries.text: The board outside the townmaster's hall has nine notices on it and four are the same notice in different hands. A woman reads it, does not take anything, and walks away. Behind her the Stonehill's chimney is going hard and the two houses either side of it are cold.

entries.label: Evening, the first day
entries.text: The light goes early and it goes fast. Doors close up and down the street, and they close before they need to. By full dark there is nobody out at all, and the only sound in Phandalin is the Stonehill, and even that is muted.
The notice board outside the hall is how work gets given out. Harbin writes the notices himself.
entries.label: The moment they reach the square

entries.text: Nobody in Phandalin will name what is wrong in the north. They will all agree that something is.
entries.label: The first time anyone asks about the north

entries.text: Two families have left in the last fortnight. Neither sold up. Both just went.
entries.label: If they ask about the empty houses
The board
entries.text: Nine notices and four of them are the same job in different hands, which means Harbin has written it out again every week and nobody has taken it.
Half the chimneys in sight are cold. Not banked, not smoking low: out. And there is fresh timber stacked against three houses that nobody is building with.
entries.label: Perception DC 10

entries.text: Everyone here is being pleasant at you and nobody is asking you to stay. They have decided, collectively and without discussing it, that strangers are a thing that happens and then leaves.
entries.label: Insight DC 11

entries.text: Phandalin has been burnt down at least twice that anyone wrote down. It gets rebuilt because of what is under it, not because anyone loves it.
entries.label: History DC 12

entries.text: Three more shutters boarded. Two more carts packed and not yet leaving.
entries.label: Perception DC 12

entries.text: Half of these were posted weeks ago and nobody has taken them.
entries.label: Investigation DC 13

options: Drink at the Stonehill and listen
Sell to Linene, or try to
Ask Halia for something she should not give you
Talk to the refugees rather than about them
Talk to whoever is packing a cart
Ask Harbin what the plan is, and keep asking
Read the board properly, all nine notices
Find out which houses are empty and why

checks.when: Standing in the square and looking around. The default.
checks.success: Half the chimneys in sight are cold. Not banked, not smoking low: out. And there is fresh timber stacked against three houses that nobody is building with.
checks.failure: A mining town in the mud. Busy enough. People glance at you and go back to work.

checks.when: Walking the streets properly rather than crossing them.
checks.success: The empty houses are not derelict. Doors shut, shutters pulled, one of them with a pot still on the step. People left, and they left recently, and they left tidily.
checks.failure: Mud, sled ruts, the usual. You would need longer.

checks.when: On the town generally, or on anyone you are talking to.
checks.success: Everyone here is being pleasant at you and nobody is asking you to stay. They have decided, collectively and without discussing it, that strangers are a thing that happens and then leaves.
checks.failure: A frontier town being frontier-polite. Hard to read past that.

checks.when: On Phandalin itself, asked of anyone or remembered.
checks.success: Phandalin has been burnt down at least twice that anyone wrote down. It gets rebuilt because of what is under it, not because anyone loves it.
checks.failure: A mining settlement. New. That is about all that is written down.

checks.when: On Harbin, while he assigns work
checks.success: He is not sending you because you are capable. He is sending you because you are not from here.
checks.failure: He is nervous, but everyone is nervous.

checks.success: Nothing she has said is a lie, and nothing she has said is the reason she is talking to you.
checks.failure: She is a shopkeeper who is good at her job.

checks.success: She stops pricing you and says the drivers will not take the north road any more.
checks.failure: She quotes you a price and waits.

checks.success: Phandalin has been destroyed before. Twice. Both times everyone thought it would not happen again.

checks.when: Walking the square on a return visit
checks.success: Three more shutters boarded. Two more carts packed and not yet leaving.

checks.when: On Harbin, in front of anyone
checks.success: He folds completely and tells you the town has forty fighting adults and no plan.
Half of these were posted weeks ago and nobody has taken them.

checks.when: Asking in the taproom about the innkeeper himself
checks.success: He came from Triboar after his brother died. He does not talk about it.
checks.failure: The ordinary version of the story, which everybody already tells.

checks.success: Her caravans have been coming in short, and not because of bandits.
checks.failure: The ordinary version of the story, which everybody already tells.

checks.when: Asking about the cart that came in from the north farms
checks.success: She arrived on a cart with no adults on it.
checks.failure: The ordinary version of the story, which everybody already tells.

cues.text: Quote everything ten percent high the first time. If they push back, drop it without comment. That is the whole prejudice, no speech.

cues.when: An old miner in the corner
cues.text: He saw elves once as a boy and has waited sixty years to tell someone. He is delighted. He is the counterweight.
Two people answer at once, differently, then look at each other.

cues.when: Once they stop explaining the cold away
cues.text: Reveal the Cryovain clock. Showing the track is itself a beat: they can suddenly see how much time is left, and the name at the top is the one nobody in town will say.

cues.when: The first time they cross the square
cues.text: Somebody is nailing boards over a north-facing window. Nobody comments on it. If asked: "Wind." It is not the wind.

cues.when: If they take a job from the board
cues.text: Harbin is relieved and shows it for exactly one second before he covers it. That flicker is the whole man. Do not explain it.

cues.when: If they ask why nobody local takes the work
cues.text: Three different people give three answers: too busy, too far, not my business. All three are lying and none of them are lying well.
One thing is worse than when they left, and it is always something domestic: fewer chimneys going, a cart being loaded, the board with more notices and fewer people reading it.

tokens.note: The notice board. Nine notices, four the same job. GIVE: item.notice if they take one down.
A crate outside Barthen's, stencilled and re-nailed. Lamp oil, the last tin in town. GIVE: item.lampoil.
Rainwater barrel at the corner of the square. A child has dropped a tarnished brooch in it. GIVE: item.brooch.
The burnt frontage at the north end. Under the fallen beam: a mason's mark, cut out of the lintel and kept. GIVE: item.markstone.
A cairn at the edge of the graveyard, built last month, no name on it. Coins left on top: 6 sp. Taking them is a choice and the town will notice.
A pack outside the Sleeping Giant, abandoned in a hurry. Bedroll, a knife, and a hand-drawn chart with farms crossed off going south. GIVE: item.chart.
A body nobody has claimed, laid in the lean-to behind the hall for the ground to thaw. Frostbitten to the bone. GIVE: item.scale if they look in the wound.
The well. Hauling the bucket up brings a silver ring on the rope. GIVE: item.ring.
A handcart loaded and roped, standing outside a shut house. Nobody has come back for it. 12 gp of household goods. Taking it is theft and the town will notice that too.

prep.want: Work, rumours, a bed that is not snow.
prep.threat: Nothing physical. Harbin will happily aim them at something lethal.
prep.wrong: Too many empty houses, and everyone has agreed not to see them.
prep.notes: The hub. Every return shows one thing worse than last time, tied to the clock rather than a schedule.

scenes.name: The Stonehill Inn
scenes.description: Two storeys, all of them warm, and the only genuinely comfortable chairs in fifty miles.

entries.label: Through the door
entries.text: The heat hits you like a hand. Somebody is playing something badly on a whistle, somebody else is telling a story they have told before, and for a moment the north is a rumour that happens to other people.
Toblen keeps the real job board. Harbin's is the one for show.
entries.label: Performance DC 12
Late, when it thins out
entries.text: The room empties in ones and twos and none of them say goodnight to each other. By the end there is an old miner in the corner who has not moved all evening and Toblen wiping a bar that is already clean, and neither of them is going anywhere.
Toblen Stonehill keeps the inn, came up from Triboar, and has never been further north than the town limit.
entries.label: When they first speak to Toblen

entries.text: Six rooms. Five made up. One slept in three weeks ago and not stripped since.
entries.label: If they take a room, or ask about one

entries.text: The taproom goes quiet when the north is mentioned and starts again on a different subject.
entries.label: The first time the north is mentioned in the taproom
The corner table
entries.text: An old miner sits in the corner and has not moved all evening. He is watching the door, not the fire.
It is too quiet for the number of people in it. Everyone is here and almost nobody is talking, and the ones who are talking are doing it too close together.
entries.label: Perception DC 10

entries.text: Toblen keeps looking at the door. Not nervously. Hopefully. He is waiting for somebody who has not come in for a while.
entries.label: Insight DC 11

entries.text: Six rooms and five of them made up. The sixth has been slept in and not stripped, and the tally by the door stops three weeks ago.
entries.label: Investigation DC 11

entries.text: Nobody sits with their back to the north window. Not one person.
entries.label: Perception DC 13

Buy a round and ask about the north
Rent rooms and take a long rest

checks.success: It is too quiet for the number of people in it. Everyone is here and almost nobody is talking, and the ones who are talking are doing it too close together.
checks.failure: A warm room, a good fire, and a landlord who is pleased to see coin.

checks.when: On Toblen, or on the room, while you drink.
checks.success: Toblen keeps looking at the door. Not nervously. Hopefully. He is waiting for somebody who has not come in for a while.
checks.failure: He is a busy man being friendly to paying strangers.

checks.when: On the taproom: the ledger, the rooms, the stock.
checks.success: Six rooms and five of them made up. The sixth has been slept in and not stripped, and the tally by the door stops three weeks ago.
checks.failure: An inn, kept well enough. Nothing out of place that you can find.

checks.success: The room turns. Advantage on the next social check anyone in the party makes tonight.

checks.failure: A warm room full of tired people.

Somebody says 'dragon' as a joke, and the room goes quiet for exactly one second too long.

scenes.name: Gnomengarde
scenes.description: A rock-gnome warren pressed into a granite hillside. Every door is slightly too short. The air smells of hot brass and burnt sugar.

entries.label: At the door
entries.text: Somewhere behind the walls a mechanism is running that nobody has turned off in years. You feel it in the floor before you hear it. A gnome opens a hatch at knee height, looks at your boots, says 'yes, good, excellent,' and closes it again.
Two kings rule here, Dabbledob and Gnerkli, and both of them want out.
entries.label: When they first meet either king

entries.text: Gnomes have gone missing. The kings will not say how many.
entries.label: Investigation DC 12

entries.text: The lower stores are sealed, and the kings sealed them.
entries.label: Investigation DC 14
When it turns
entries.text: Gnerkli has stopped talking. He is looking at the barred door and he is not looking at you, and when he finally speaks it is not an answer to anything you asked. He says: 'It was already in there. I only stopped it getting out.'

entries.label: The rope bridge over the falls
entries.text: The cavern opens and the sound arrives first: water falling a long way into water. A rope bridge crosses the gorge, and on the far side there are crates stacked six high, a long table laid for thirty with candles burning down, and nobody sitting at it. Below the bridge, an island of blue crystal glows under the mist and lights the whole chamber from underneath.

entries.label: The red shrine, west side
entries.text: Past the pillars on the left there is a rug the colour of arterial blood and a plinth with a crystal on it that is the wrong colour for everything else down here. Four braziers burn around it. Somebody tends them. Nobody will say who.

entries.label: At the long table
entries.text: Thirty places, thirty plates, and food on maybe eleven of them. The candles have been lit and relit so often the table is welded to itself with wax. The gnomes sit where they always sat and nobody sits in the gaps.
The blue crystal island under the bridge lights the whole warren and has never been mined. Cutting it is forbidden and nobody remembers who forbade it.

entries.text: The red crystal on the west plinth was brought in from outside. It is the only red thing in Gnomengarde.

scenes.name: Umbrage Hill
scenes.description: A windmill on a bare hill, and a great deal of blood in the snow that will not wash out until spring.

entries.label: After the fight
entries.text: It is over, and the hill is very quiet. Adabra Gwynn comes out with a bucket, looks at the thing in the snow, looks at you, and says: 'It came down the hill. Nothing comes down that hill.'
Adabra Gwynn lives here alone and midwifes for the whole region.

entries.text: The wind comes over the rise hard enough to lean on. The mill sails are turning, unloaded, which means nobody has set the brake, which means nobody has been out here today. Halfway up you pass the standing stones, and then you see the shape in the grass on the downhill side.

entries.label: At the carcass
entries.text: It is a manticore, and it is enormous, and it is intact. Lion body, bat wings, and the ruin of a face that was almost human. Nothing has fed on it. Nothing has even landed on it. Frost on the grass around it has not melted where it lies.

entries.label: At the mill door
entries.text: The door opens before you knock. A woman in her forties with flour to the elbow looks at four armed elves on her step and says, "You are not from the town." It is not a question and it is not hostile. It is a woman working out how much of her afternoon this is going to cost.
Adabra Gwynn is a herbalist and midwife. Half of Phandalin owes her something and none of them come out here.

scenes.name: The Dwarven Excavation
scenes.description: A hillside opened like a wound, three dwarves living in it, and a great deal of very old stonework behind them.

entries.label: Over the ridge
entries.text: There is a hole in the hill somebody made on purpose, and shoring timbers going into it much newer than the stone they hold up. A dwarf stands on a crate arguing with two others about whether the crate is load-bearing.
What they have broken into is older than the mine, and older than the dwarves who built the mine.

entries.text: The lantern reaches the far wall and the wall is not dwarven. The stone is dressed differently, jointed differently, and it has been standing here in the dark long enough that the dwarves' own two-hundred-year-old work looks like scaffolding against it.

scenes.name: Falcon's Hunting Lodge
scenes.description: A well-built lodge where a well-built lodge has no business being, with a man outside it listening to the treeline rather than to you.

entries.label: Falcon, when it lands
entries.text: He does not look surprised. That is the thing you notice. Everyone else in this valley has been surprised for a month, and this man has not been, and has not been for some time.

entries.text: He does not sleep. Some time after midnight you find him on the porch with a bow across his knees, looking north at nothing in particular, and he says, without turning round: 'It goes over about now. Most nights.'

entries.label: When they come
entries.text: They do not sneak. The first you know of it is a hymn, sung badly and loudly by several voices from the treeline, and then the air above the lodge roof turns the colour of a bruise. Falcon puts down the cup he is holding and says, without any particular urgency: 'Get away from the windows.'
Anchorites of Talos have been attacking the lodge. They are orcs, and they are praying.

scenes.name: The Long Span
scenes.description: An elvish viaduct three tiers high, half fallen, standing in forest a mile off the Gnomengarde road. The road it carried does not go anywhere any more.

entries.label: First sight, from the track
entries.text: The trees open and the thing is simply there, which is worse than coming upon it gradually. Three tiers of white stone arches marching out of the forest and stopping in mid-air, with copper roofing gone green on the towers and a stair cut up the near pier. Steam or cloud comes off the broken end in a way that weather does not explain. Nothing about it is ruined the way the rest of this country is ruined. It is ruined the way something is ruined on purpose.

entries.label: At the foot of the stair
entries.text: The stair is cut into the pier itself, not built against it, and the treads are worn in the middle by feet that stopped using them a very long time ago. Somebody has swept them. Not recently. But once, and after the fall.

entries.label: The first tier
entries.text: Wide enough for two carts. Ivy in the joins, saplings in the cracks, and against the parapet a row of shallow stone niches, most of them empty. Water runs somewhere inside the stonework and has never stopped.

entries.label: The second tier
entries.text: Higher, colder, and you can see over the treetops now. Halfway along, the span is broken through and the gap is thirty feet of nothing with the forest floor a long way below. Somebody laid planks across it. The planks are old and they are not elvish.
The Long Span is elvish work and older than any settlement in the valley. The joins are too tight to get a knife into.

cues.when: If they walk past without climbing
cues.text: Let them. Nothing follows. Two days later somebody in Phandalin mentions that the span used to have a warden, and that is the whole hook re-offered, for free.

cues.text: A sound from a long way up: metal on stone, once, and then nothing. Do not explain it. Do not repeat it for at least ten minutes of table time.

cues.when: On the first and second tiers
cues.text: Small finds only. A coin in a niche, a knife in a crack, a pack somebody abandoned. Nothing fights them below the top. The climb is the tension and the emptiness is the point.
He is standing at the broken end with his back to them, and he has been standing there a long time. He turns when they are close enough that running is a choice rather than a reflex.
Any object, sincerely offered, staggers him. He has not been given anything in three hundred years. It does not end the fight, but it buys a round and it changes what the fight is about.

He does not kill. He puts people down and steps over them. Drop a character to 0 and he moves to the next, and he will not strike a creature that is already down. Say so with his actions, never in narration.
He kneels, which is not surrender: it is the posture of somebody being relieved of duty. Then the armour is empty and it was always going to be empty.

prep.want: To be relieved. He cannot leave the span and he cannot stop holding it, and he has forgotten how to say either of those things.
prep.threat: Real but bounded. He will beat the party unconscious. He will not kill them and he cannot follow them down.
prep.wrong: The span was cut deliberately, from above, by the people who built it. He is still collecting a toll for a road that was destroyed by his own side.
prep.notes: Optional, on the way back from Gnomengarde, and it is meant to be skippable. If the party walk past, nothing punishes them and the hook comes back cheaply in town. If they climb, give them two tiers of quiet and small finds before anything happens: the emptiness is what makes the top land. The fight is the session's only real danger and it has a hard floor — nobody dies on this bridge. He fights to unconsciousness and steps over the fallen. Offer him something and he falters. Beat him and the armour is empty, and has been for a very long time.

stages.playerText: The gnomes of Gnomengarde have stopped trading with Phandalin. Find out why.
stages.dmText: Harbin thinks it is a trade dispute, which is what he would think. It is not. Four gnomes are missing and the warren has collectively agreed not to notice, and the thing that took them is still inside.

options.label: They leave it and come back later

stages.playerText: A warren of workshops behind a waterfall, a rope bridge over a gorge lit from below by blue crystal, and a long table laid for thirty with eleven places used.
stages.dmText: Play the gnomes as delighted and busy and entirely unwilling to be asked a direct question. Every corridor has a device in it and a third of them are broken at chest height, in a line, which is a trail if anyone follows it.

options.label: They open the sealed door first

stages.playerText: Four gnomes are unaccounted for, and the kings knew the number without being told.
stages.dmText: Gnerkli can name all four. He will, separated from Dabbledob and asked kindly.

stages.playerText: The lower stores are barred from the outside. Somebody here did that on purpose.
stages.dmText: Reveal the mimic's presence when the door opens. Identity later, if ever. Adhesive on the paladin first.

stages.playerText: Gnerkli sealed the door himself, and kept sending gnomes past it.
stages.dmText: He is not evil. He was frightened and the fright made him useless. Let the party price that.

options.label: They deal with the thing below
They expose him to the warren

stages.playerText: It is dead. There are four sets of tools inside it.
stages.dmText: Give the tools names. The gnomes will want them back and will not be able to say why.

stages.playerText: Gnomengarde has no government, and it is partly your doing.
stages.dmText: A consequence, not a punishment. The warren still helps them, badly, with nobody in charge.

stages.playerText: Gnomengarde trades with Phandalin again, and there are four empty places at the long table.
stages.dmText: The gnomes will not stop laying those places. Do not have them grieve on screen. The reward is access: they will make, fix, or modify one thing for the party per visit, for free, forever, and never mention why. PAYS OUT: Harbin pays 75 gp for reopening the trade. The gnomes give a far-lens and a coil of self-knotting rope on the spot (GIVE item.lens, item.rope) and from now on will make, fix or modify one thing per visit for free, forever, and never say why. If the party found the four sets of tools in the mimic, those are the dead gnomes' and handing them back matters more than keeping them (item.tools).

stages.playerText: Beds, bowls, coats, places at the table. The number is wrong by four and nobody corrects it.
stages.dmText: The reveal, and it should land quietly rather than as a gotcha. If a player counts anything at all, give it to them. The correct response from the nearest gnome is to lay another place at the table and carry on talking.

stages.playerText: Gnerkli is not evading you. He is waiting to be asked a direct question by somebody kind.
stages.dmText: He knows. He has known for two weeks. He has not said because saying it makes it real and because he is the one who screwed the doors shut. Ask him gently and the whole thing comes out in one go.

stages.playerText: The storage chest in the lower hall is not a storage chest.
stages.dmText: The mimic. It has been eating gnomes one at a time and it is patient. It only attacks something that touches it, which means the party can walk past it forever and so could the gnomes, which is exactly how four of them went.

stages.playerText: The dwarves at the Dwarven Excavation have stopped sending word. Dorn Tradesmith wants to know whether his people are alive.
stages.dmText: A day east. The dig is fine; the dwarves are alive and working. What has gone wrong is smaller and stranger than anyone expects, and the payload is what is under the dwarven layer, not who is hurt.

options.label: They leave it and come back later

stages.playerText: A trench driven into a hillside, shored in a hurry at the deep end, and three dwarves working in near silence.
stages.dmText: Don-Jon Raskin runs the dig and is proud of it. He will feed them and show them everything above the shoring. Below it he changes the subject, twice, and then admits they stopped digging because of what the stone did.

stages.playerText: The stonework changes hands halfway down, and the older half is elvish.
stages.dmText: Free payoff for an all-elf party. Don-Jon knew and said nothing.

options.label: They leave it and come back later

stages.playerText: Paid, in ore, slightly better than agreed.
stages.dmText: Don-Jon hands over the survey map. The second drawing on it is not in his handwriting.

options.label: They press him about the map
They take the pay and go

stages.playerText: He admits the dig was never about ore.
stages.dmText: He was following the older plan. He does not know who drew it. Hook to the Woodland Manse.

stages.playerText: The dig is safe, and there is something under it that is older than the people who hired you.
stages.dmText: Dorn pays. The thread that matters is the elvish stonework: it connects to the manse, the Circle, the barrow and the undercroft under the hold. Note the date they learned it. This is the campaign's second spine and it is not about the dragon at all. PAYS OUT: Dorn Tradesmith pays 100 gp on delivery of the news. Don-Jon's crew hand over a cask of dwarven ale and a surveyor's map of the dig (GIVE item.dwarfale, item.map). If the party went below the dwarven layer, they also leave with the mason's mark (item.markstone) and the knowledge that the elvish work is older — that thread runs to the manse, the Circle, the barrow and the undercroft.

stages.playerText: Below the dwarven cut the stonework changes: older, finer, elvish, and the joins are too tight to get a knife into.
stages.dmText: Elvish work under a dwarven dig, and the elvish is the better stonework by a long way. Nobody at this table expects that. Let a History check land it and let the dwarves be embarrassed rather than secretive — they are not hiding it, they are superstitious about it.

stages.playerText: Something came up the cut that is not a rockfall.
stages.dmText: The ochre jelly, if it happens. Slashing splits it, and any Arcana check warns them first. If the party skip the fight entirely by listening to the warning, that is a win and should be paid like one.

stages.playerText: Harbin has posted work: somebody should ride out to Umbrage Hill and check on Adabra Gwynn, the midwife. It is an hour north and nobody local has taken the job in three weeks.
stages.dmText: This is the session-one job and it is not a monster hunt, whatever the notice implies. The manticore is already dead on the hillside when they arrive. The job is: get there, find the body, meet the woman, and come back carrying a question. Harbin will pay 50 gp and will not ask what they found. If they press him for detail before they go, he has none — he has not been out of the hall in a month.

stages.playerText: Whatever came at you on the hill is down.
stages.dmText: Only if the party made a fight. There is no scheduled combat here. If they drew on Adabra she shuts the door and the job ends badly with nobody hurt. If they poked the stones, one hungry pack came off the ridge and broke when it lost two.

stages.playerText: The manticore was not killed by anything that wanted to eat it. Nothing has touched the body since. There is a scale in the wound that does not belong to it.
stages.dmText: This is the hinge of the whole campaign and they pulled it themselves an hour outside town. Give them the scale as a physical object. Do not name the dragon, do not have anyone in Phandalin name it either. The frost scale plus the empty road plus the view from the mill cap is enough for the table to work it out, and them working it out is worth more than you telling them.

options.label: They go up the mill to look north

stages.playerText: Adabra Gwynn owes you, and she is not leaving her hill.
stages.dmText: She becomes the party's healer of last resort, at her house, on her terms, for free. Harbin pays without asking questions. If they brought the scale back and showed anyone in town, note who saw it: that person starts behaving differently the next time the party are in Phandalin. PAYS OUT: Harbin pays 50 gp from the town chest, no questions. Adabra gives them her tonic and frost salve free, now and for the rest of the campaign (GIVE item.tonic, item.frostsalve), and will treat any wound at her house at no charge. If they brought the scale back, that is the campaign's first real lead and costs them nothing. XP: treat as one medium encounter even with no fight.

stages.playerText: A windmill turning with nobody working it, a ring of standing stones on the slope, and something dead in the grass.
stages.dmText: Let them choose their order: body first or door first. Body first and they meet Adabra already unsettled by armed strangers examining a corpse in her yard. Door first and she tells them about it herself, flatly, having not gone to look. Either is correct. Neither is a trap.

stages.playerText: Adabra Gwynn is alive, working, and has had her shutters closed for two days.
stages.dmText: She will not leave. The first refusal is flat and reasonless. The second, if asked kindly, gets the truth: her mother is buried under the mill floor and she is not leaving her. That is the whole emotional payload of session one and it costs nothing but a second ask.

options.label: They go and look at the body

stages.playerText: From the cap of the mill you can see the whole valley, and there is no smoke north of Umbrage Hill at all.
stages.dmText: The free reveal. If they never climb up, have Adabra take them up to explain why she will not go south either. Scale of the problem, delivered as geography rather than exposition.

stages.playerText: Orcs have taken a ranch on the south road.
stages.dmText: They are refugees with axes. That does not make them safe. Orcs holding a ranch they retreated into, not raided. Talking works and gets better information than killing does. Yargath saw the thing land and will describe it accurately if asked before steel comes out.

stages.playerText: The orcs are dead, and one was already dying of the cold.
stages.dmText: The frostbite wound is the clue. Do not point at it. Orcs holding a ranch they retreated into, not raided. Talking works and gets better information than killing does. Yargath saw the thing land and will describe it accurately if asked before steel comes out.

options.label: They leave it and come back later

stages.playerText: Yargath talks. His people are running from the same thing.
stages.dmText: He describes it plainly and without drama, which is what makes it land.

stages.playerText: There are armed orcs somewhere in the valley who owe you.
stages.dmText: Bring them back at clock seven. They will not save the town, but they will hold a gate.

options.label: They leave it and come back later

stages.playerText: An unsent letter, and a farmer who stayed for the cattle.
stages.dmText: Narth will not take the letter back if they show it to him. Orcs holding a ranch they retreated into, not raided. Talking works and gets better information than killing does. Yargath saw the thing land and will describe it accurately if asked before steel comes out.

options.label: They search the rest of the house

stages.playerText: The upper floor has two small beds in it, and the cellar has a blanket and a candle stub on the floor.
stages.dmText: His family hid in the cellar and then left for Neverwinter. He was out at the far fence when the orcs came, and he has not been down there since. Do not have him explain any of it — let the party assemble it from a slate, four beds and some crumbs, and then decide whether to say anything to him.

stages.playerText: You asked him where he was.
stages.dmText: This is the only question he cannot answer. He tells them about the cattle again. If a player waits through the silence rather than filling it, he says it: he was at the far fence, and he was not here.

stages.playerText: Butterskull Ranch is standing, and Narth is still in it.
stages.dmText: He is the face of the evacuation argument later. Orcs holding a ranch they retreated into, not raided. Talking works and gets better information than killing does. Yargath saw the thing land and will describe it accurately if asked before steel comes out. PAYS OUT: 100 gp from the town chest. Off the ranch itself: gauntlets of ogre power (GIVE item.gauntlets), an unsent letter (item.letter), a child's slate (item.slate), and the white scale from the orc's wound (item.dragonscale). If they talked to Yargath rather than killing him, they also get an accurate description of the dragon and a witness who will say it out loud in Phandalin.

stages.playerText: Tibor Wester needs the timber camp cleared. He is Harbin's cousin.
stages.dmText: There is an ankheg. There is also a crew that walked out. A crew that walked out and a foreman who did not tell his cousin. The ankheg is the surface problem. The real one is that Tibor has been lying to the townmaster for eleven days.

stages.playerText: Half the crew left a week ago and Tibor told nobody.
stages.dmText: He is not corrupt, only ashamed. Let them decide whether Harbin hears about it.

options.label: They leave it and come back later

stages.playerText: The camp is safe and the timber is stacked.
stages.dmText: Timber matters at clock seven: it is what Axeholm's gates get repaired with.

stages.playerText: Phandalin has timber.
stages.dmText: Cash this in during the evacuation. A crew that walked out and a foreman who did not tell his cousin. The ankheg is the surface problem. The real one is that Tibor has been lying to the townmaster for eleven days. PAYS OUT: 75 gp from Harbin. Out of the ankheg's burrow: 55 gp and the logger's tally stick (GIVE item.tallystick). Tibor gives them his own 18 gp to keep quiet and they should be allowed to refuse it. The crew's half of the tally stick is the proof he knew early.

stages.playerText: There is a dwarven fortress to the west with its doors still shut.
stages.dmText: Plant this early in any table conversation. It becomes the evacuation site.

options.label: They leave it and come back later

stages.playerText: The gate is barred from the inside, and the fortress is empty.
stages.dmText: Animated armour guarding a line. A shade in the cistern. Icehewer below.

stages.playerText: Four keys. Three fit doors you have seen.
stages.dmText: The fourth opens the cistern. Say nothing. A fortress barred from inside by people who then left another way. Everything here is a puzzle with the answer visible on the floor. Reward walking round rather than through.

options.label: They leave it and come back later

stages.playerText: Axeholm is empty, defensible, and yours if you want it.
stages.dmText: The moment the clock hits six, somebody should remember this room.

options.label: They propose it as a refuge

stages.playerText: Phandalin has somewhere to go.
stages.dmText: This is the party choosing to save people instead of killing a thing. Reward it hard.

stages.playerText: Axeholm is known, and the only defensible place for forty miles.
stages.dmText: A fortress barred from inside by people who then left another way. Everything here is a puzzle with the answer visible on the floor. Reward walking round rather than through. PAYS OUT: 125 gp for clearing it, paid by Harbin out of what is left of the town chest. Inside: 115 gp in the gate and armoury boxes, dwarf-cut bracers (GIVE item.bracers), Axeholm's keyring (item.keys), and a hunting horn (item.warhorn). The fortress becomes a place the town can fall back to, which is worth more than the coin and nobody will realise until later.

stages.playerText: Phandalin is moving to Axeholm.
stages.dmText: Slow, cold, and the best thing they will do all campaign. Keep the clock running.

stages.playerText: Harbin will not order it. He says it would look like panic.
stages.dmText: He is not wrong, and it will kill people. Let the party go around him if they think of it.

stages.playerText: An elven house in the woods, left rather than lost.
stages.dmText: Every player at this table is an elf. This is their scene. Elvish, older than the Woods, and every window faces north because they were watching for something. The spellbook is the prize; the fourth hand in it is the thread.

options.label: They leave it and come back later

stages.playerText: Nothing was taken. The cups are still out.
stages.dmText: Whoever lived here left in order, deliberately, and expected to come back.

stages.playerText: A spellbook, and one page in a hand nobody recognises.
stages.dmText: Older than the book, and matching the second drawing on Don-Jon's map.

stages.playerText: They took nothing, and that was a decision.
stages.dmText: Honour it. The house opens something later that it would not have if they had looted it.

stages.playerText: They know something about their own people that Phandalin never will.
stages.dmText: Elvish, older than the Woods, and every window faces north because they were watching for something. The spellbook is the prize; the fourth hand in it is the thread. PAYS OUT: no one is paying for this one, so the house is the payment. 64 gp in the flooded room, a water-damaged spellbook (GIVE item.spellbook), a plain silver ring (item.ring), a bone comb (item.comb) and a cup off the table (item.cup). The spellbook's fourth hand is the thread; do not explain it this campaign.

quests.title: Something came down off the peak

stages.playerText: Animals are moving south early this year.
stages.dmText: Seed in scene description only. Never let an NPC announce it.

options.label: A player says it out loud

stages.playerText: The manticore was fleeing, not hunting.
stages.dmText: Pays off session one retroactively, and costs nothing. The spine. Do not advance this on a schedule — advance it when the party learn something, and let the clock carry the pressure in between. Never name Cryovain before the players do.

stages.playerText: Farms in the north are empty. Nessa came on a cart with no adults on it.
stages.dmText: She describes the sound before the shape. Use her properly once, then keep her in the background.

stages.playerText: The orcs are not raiding. They are homeless, and they are angry at a god about it.
stages.dmText: Butterskull, the loggers' camp, the shrine, the circle, the lodge — every orc in this campaign lost the same mountain. When the party assembles that themselves, Icespire Hold stops being a location and becomes an answer.

options.label: They work out what took the mountain

stages.playerText: It has a name, and the older locals already knew it.
stages.dmText: The real reveal is that Phandalin has been quietly not talking about this for weeks.

options.label: They decide to leave the valley

stages.playerText: Phandalin is moving to Axeholm.
stages.dmText: Harder, slower, and worth far more than a fight. Let the clock keep running while they do it.

stages.playerText: Icespire Hold. It sleeps on the upper level, where the roof used to be.
stages.dmText: Not before level 5 or clock seven. Three levels: the orcs' ground floor, which is empty and says why; the roofless level above, where it sleeps in a hollow of pressed snow; and the undercroft below, which nobody up there ever went down to look at.

stages.playerText: You decided this is not yours to solve.
stages.dmText: Legitimate. Run the evacuation instead, and let the dragon be weather rather than a boss.

stages.playerText: There is a crypt under the fortress and everybody in it is an elf.
stages.dmText: The third sighting of the older hand, and the answer to a question nobody asked: the orcs' stronghold was built on a graveyard, and the graveyard was sealed from the inside. Do not resolve it. If your elf party wants to do something for their own dead before they go up and fight, let them, and let it matter.

stages.playerText: No roof, knee-deep snow, and a hollow in it that is still warm.
stages.dmText: It is close and it already knows. Ice Walk means it moves through this at full speed and they do not. Give them one clean chance to leave and mean it.

stages.playerText: You arranged the ground before you called it down.
stages.dmText: Reward every piece of preparation explicitly — gnomish pitch, the hidden climb, Falcon on a ledge, the orcs Yargath owes them. This is what four sessions of groundwork was for.

stages.playerText: It is over, one way or the other.
stages.dmText: Under 66 hp it commits. Under 30 it leaves, and it remembers faces. If it flees, it is not an anticlimax — it is the second half, and Phandalin has to decide what to do in the meantime. PAYS OUT: 220 gp from the hoard, a hunting horn (GIVE item.warhorn), Icehewer if they have not already taken it from the barrow (item.icehewer), and the valley stops emptying. Phandalin survives the winter. That is the campaign.

stages.playerText: You walked away from it a second time.
stages.dmText: Legitimate, and the clock keeps running. Let Axeholm fill with people.

stages.playerText: Halia offered help, and did not ask for anything.
stages.dmText: She means it. Do not telegraph a trap, because there is not one yet.

stages.playerText: You took it.
stages.dmText: Wait at least three sessions, then she asks for something small and entirely reasonable.

stages.playerText: You did not take it. She was not offended, which was somehow worse.
stages.dmText: She helps Phandalin publicly instead, and now the town owes her rather than the party. PAYS OUT: nothing, and she is perfectly pleasant about it, which should worry them more than anger would.

stages.playerText: She wants something small, and entirely reasonable.
stages.dmText: Small and reasonable is the point. The Zhentarim never open with anything else.

stages.playerText: The debt is settled, and she says so warmly.
stages.dmText: It is not settled. She now has something on them and something on the town. PAYS OUT: 120 gp, well over the job's worth, which is the point. She wanted something she did not mention and she got it.

stages.playerText: You told her no. She said 'of course' and meant something by it.
stages.dmText: The Zhentarim do not retaliate. They wait, and they help somebody else instead. PAYS OUT: nothing, and the Zhentarim now know their names.

stages.playerText: Escort a new overseer to the Mountain's Toe. The pay is good and the job is dull.
stages.dmText: It is neither. Don-Jon Raskin has not been told why the last overseer left.

stages.playerText: The mine is tidy, stocked, and empty of people.
stages.dmText: Wererats. Three of them, and they will talk first if given the chance.

stages.playerText: Your weapons are sliding off them.
stages.dmText: Say it plainly on the first hit. The fight turns into the conversation the moment they understand.

options.label: They find silver and finish it

stages.playerText: They were driven out of the Shrine of Savras by orcs. They want it back.
stages.dmText: They keep their word. A monster that honours a bargain teaches this table more than one that betrays them.

stages.playerText: You have promised them a shrine.
stages.dmText: This opens the Shrine of Savras, and it is the second time the party hears that orcs displaced somebody.

stages.playerText: The wererats moved out. The mine is working.
stages.dmText: Don-Jon owes them, Phandalin has gold again, and the party has an odd, reliable ally in the hills. PAYS OUT: the wererats hand over 90 gp and the mine, and keep their word. The party get less coin and a standing arrangement, which is the better outcome and should be paid as one.

stages.playerText: You promised and did not go.
stages.dmText: The wererats stay. They do not retaliate — they simply never help again, and the party will feel that later. PAYS OUT: nothing, and the mine stays shut. Say so plainly rather than softening it.

stages.playerText: The mine is clear and there is a great deal of blood in it.
stages.dmText: Legitimate. But the shrine thread never opens, and the orc picture stays blurry for longer. PAYS OUT: 150 gp from the mine's own paychest and 30 gp of ore in the cart. GIVE: item.healer, item.lantern, item.silverdagger off the dead miner.

stages.playerText: Barthen has not heard from Falcon in a fortnight and would like someone to look.
stages.dmText: Elmar is the only person who calls him Gustaf. Do not explain that; let a player ask.

stages.playerText: The lodge is standing, and the man in it is not surprised to see anyone.
stages.dmText: Falcon is calm because he has been expecting worse than visitors.

options.label: They go up to the loft

stages.playerText: Orcs in soaked robes, singing, and the sky above the roof going wrong.
stages.dmText: Two anchorites and some orcs. If the table is thin, one anchorite and let Falcon hold a door.

stages.playerText: There is a month of stores in his loft and a north shutter worn pale from being opened.
stages.dmText: The clearest evidence in the campaign that one person saw this coming and told nobody. He is not hiding it — nobody has ever come up here to look. If they find it before the attack, the attack lands differently: he was right.

options.label: They ask him what he is watching for

stages.playerText: The lodge stands. Falcon is talking now.
stages.dmText: The attack is what opens him up. Icespire Hold comes out of this conversation, not out of a check.

options.label: They ask him about the dragon

stages.playerText: He has seen one before. He says so plainly, and then says where this one sleeps.
stages.dmText: The single most useful piece of information in the campaign, given freely, because they earned it by standing in his yard. PAYS OUT: Falcon has no coin and says so. He gives his climber's kit, his spare shafts and a whistle he will answer (GIVE item.climbkit, item.shafts, item.whistle), and he goes up the mountain with them when they finally go — which is the reward, and it is a better one than money.

stages.playerText: There is a shrine north of the road, and orcs are sitting in it.
stages.dmText: Two doors in: the wererats' bargain, or greed. Either is fine.

stages.playerText: Orcs hold it. The woman who kept it is still alive.
stages.dmText: They spared Miraal because she is touched by a god. Not theirs, but a god.

options.label: They talk to the anchorite first

stages.playerText: The orcs tell them what happened to their mountain.
stages.dmText: The third telling. By now the party should be assembling it themselves.

stages.playerText: The shrine is quiet and Miraal is still in it.
stages.dmText: She becomes the one person who can tell them where the dragon is without them having to go and look. PAYS OUT: 33 gp from the offering chest that the Anchorite will not touch, a flask of holy water (GIVE item.holywater), and one true answer from the font (item.prophecy). Answer the question honestly at the table even if it wrecks your plan.

stages.playerText: You left them in it.
stages.dmText: Defensible. The wererats do not get their home, and they will remember that. PAYS OUT: nothing, and the font stays unasked. The Anchorite is still there if they come back.

stages.playerText: Somebody has been asking in Phandalin whether anyone has heard thunder without weather.
stages.dmText: Talon is looking for help and it costs her to ask. The ring holds something out and has for longer than anyone counts. Do not resolve it this campaign. Note who damages a stone.

stages.playerText: Anchorites in a ring of standing stones, and thunder arriving before the gesture.
stages.dmText: They are calling Gorthok. The stones are the instrument. The ring holds something out and has for longer than anyone counts. Do not resolve it this campaign. Note who damages a stone.

stages.playerText: Something the size of a cart walks into the ring, and the ground reports it.
stages.dmText: CR 7. Do not fight it. The stones are still the answer — say so in the fiction.

stages.playerText: The thunder stops. The quiet afterwards is enormous.
stages.dmText: Give the table three full seconds of nothing before anyone speaks. PAYS OUT: 36 gp left at the ring over the years, and a circle stone warm in a closed hand (GIVE item.stonering). It works only inside the valley and no one can identify it, on purpose.

stages.playerText: You left, and it is still out there.
stages.dmText: Fine. Gorthok wanders. Put it somewhere later, once, at a distance, and never explain it. PAYS OUT: nothing, and Gorthok is still out there. No penalty; note it and move on.

quests.title: What the shrine was before
quests.giver: Nobody. The bones are just there.

stages.playerText: There are old bones in the rubble of the outer wall. Decades old.
stages.dmText: The orcs moved into a place that was already a grave. Nobody in Phandalin knows what happened here, including Harbin, and Miraal answers the question in the wrong order.

stages.playerText: She answers a question you did not ask, about something that has not happened.
stages.dmText: Write down exactly what she says. It will be correct about the endgame and useless right now. That is the whole point of her.

stages.playerText: You wrote it down.
stages.dmText: Bring it back at clock seven, word for word. It should land as inevitable rather than as a trick. PAYS OUT: nothing, and the Anchorite keeps what he knows a little longer.

stages.playerText: The bones stay where they are.
stages.dmText: Fine. Leave the thread. An unanswered question in a campaign is not a loose end, it is furniture. PAYS OUT: no coin. What they get is the connection — the shrine's older stonework is the same hand as the excavation, the manse and the undercroft (GIVE item.markstone if they have not got one). This is a knowledge reward and should be given as one, out loud.

clocks.name: Cryovain
clocks.caption: What the winter does while they are busy elsewhere.
clocks.note: Show the track once they have stopped explaining it away.

events.playerText: Game is scarce. The woods are quiet in a way that is wrong.
events.dmText: Already happened: the manticore. Do not explain it.

events.playerText: A trapline is found frozen solid, animals still in it.
events.dmText: Cold damage, no claw marks. It flew over. It did not land.
Nessa. Use her properly once, then keep her in the background of every town scene.

events.playerText: Livestock killed and left. Split open, not eaten.
events.dmText: Territory, not feeding. Let somebody say that aloud and be wrong about what it means.

events.playerText: A well freezes solid overnight, inside the palisade.
events.dmText: Where it stops being a rural problem.

events.playerText: It is seen. Daylight, over the rooftops, unhurried.
events.dmText: No attack. It looks at them and leaves. Falcon arrives that night without being asked.

events.playerText: Harbin orders an evacuation and is ignored.
events.dmText: The town splits. Halia's price becomes visible. Spared orcs, if any, arrive here.
Level 5+ only. If the clock arrives early, tick seven stretches as long as you need.

clocks.name: Phandalin's nerve
clocks.caption: How much the town has left in it.

events.playerText: People are talking about the north, quietly.
The job board has more work than there are people to take it.
events.dmText: Harbin is posting jobs he knows nobody will accept.

events.playerText: Two families have left for Neverwinter.
events.dmText: The Kirks and the Trennets, both from the north side of the square. Emmet Kirk went ahead in the first week and never arrived, which is the body in the region and the purse. The party have met his widow at the notice board whether they noticed or not. Say both names.

events.playerText: The Lionshield Coster stops taking deliveries.
events.dmText: Linene is frightened and covering it with rudeness.

events.playerText: Somebody proposes paying it off. In cattle. Seriously.
events.dmText: Let the party explain why that will not work, and watch the room not believe them.

events.playerText: Half of Phandalin is packed and waiting on the road.
events.dmText: If nothing has been done by here the stakes evaporate. Force a confrontation before this.
